items.stem: 2-Propanol is oxidized at 0 degC using either PCC in CH2Cl2 or Jones reagent (CrO3/H2SO4 in aqueous acetone). Because the substrate is a secondary alcohol, both reagents stop at the same oxidation state. What is the major product?
items.why: Secondary alcohols oxidize to ketones, and ketones cannot be further oxidized under these conditions because they lack an H on the carbonyl carbon. So the choice of PCC (anhydrous, stops at aldehyde for primary) vs. Jones (aqueous, goes to acid for primary) is irrelevant for a secondary alcohol; both give the same ketone, acetone.

items.stem: tert-Butanol is heated to 90 degC in concentrated H2SO4 with no nucleophile present. The protonated alcohol loses water to form a tertiary carbocation, which loses a beta-proton in an E1 elimination. What is the principal organic product?
items.why: Hot concentrated H2SO4 dehydrates tertiary alcohols by E1: protonation of OH, loss of water to give a stable tertiary carbocation, then deprotonation of a beta-CH3 by the conjugate base. The tert-butyl cation has only one type of beta-H (all three CH3 groups are equivalent), so the only possible alkene is isobutylene (2-methylpropene).

items.stem: A Williamson ether synthesis to form an unsymmetrical ether (R-O-R') requires the alkoxide to attack the alkyl halide via SN2. The alkyl halide should therefore have minimal steric hindrance to maximize ether yield over alkene formation. Which combination is preferred?
items.why: When making an unsymmetrical ether by Williamson, dissect it so that the alkyl halide carries the less hindered alkyl group (primary or methyl) and the alkoxide carries the bulkier group. Primary halides allow clean SN2 with minimal E2 competition, so this pairing maximizes ether yield. Aryl halides fail entirely because their sp2 carbon cannot undergo backside SN2.

items.stem: An aldehyde is treated with 2 equivalents of ethanol and a catalytic amount of p-TsOH in dry benzene with a Dean-Stark trap to remove water. What functional group is present in the major product?
choices: Acetal (two OR groups on the same carbon)
items.why: Acid-catalyzed reaction of an aldehyde with 2 equivalents of alcohol gives an acetal: the first ROH adds to give a hemiacetal, the OH is then protonated and lost as water (driven by the Dean-Stark trap), and a second ROH adds to give R-CH(OR')2. Removing water with the Dean-Stark trap is the key shift that pushes the equilibrium past the hemiacetal to the acetal.

items.stem: Two molecules of acetone are combined with a catalytic amount of dilute NaOH at 25 degC, then warmed to 60 degC. What sequence of products best describes this aldol process?
choices: Diacetone alcohol (beta-hydroxy ketone), which dehydrates on heating to mesityl oxide
items.why: NaOH deprotonates one acetone at the alpha-carbon to form an enolate, which attacks the carbonyl of a second acetone, giving the beta-hydroxy ketone diacetone alcohol (4-hydroxy-4-methyl-2-pentanone). On heating, E1cb dehydration loses the beta-OH (as water) to form the alpha,beta-unsaturated ketone mesityl oxide. This two-step aldol addition-then-condensation is the classic acetone aldol.

items.stem: Propanal is stirred with 2 equivalents of ethanol and a catalytic amount of HCl in dry benzene with molecular sieves to absorb water. What is the functional class of the major isolated product?
choices: Acetal (two OR groups on the same carbon)
items.why: Under acid catalysis with 2 equivalents of alcohol and a water scavenger, an aldehyde forms an acetal: protonation, addition of ROH, loss of water (driven by the molecular sieves), and addition of a second ROH gives R-CH(OR')2. Without water removal, the equilibrium would favor the starting aldehyde plus alcohol over the acetal.

items.stem: 2-Butanone is treated with 1.0 equivalent of LiAlH4 in dry THF at 0 degC, followed by aqueous workup. Hydride is delivered to the carbonyl carbon and the alkoxide is protonated. What functional group results?
items.why: LiAlH4 delivers hydride to the carbonyl carbon, and aqueous workup protonates the alkoxide. Reduction of a ketone gives a secondary alcohol because the resulting carbon bears one H (from hydride) and two carbon substituents (from the original ketone); aldehydes give primary alcohols; esters give primary alcohols; only addition of two carbon nucleophiles to an ester would give a tertiary alcohol.

items.stem: Propanal is treated with 1.1 equivalents of ethylmagnesium bromide (EtMgBr) in dry diethyl ether at 0 degC, followed by aqueous NH4Cl workup. The carbanion adds once to the carbonyl carbon. What functional group results?
items.why: Grignard addition to an aldehyde gives a secondary alcohol: the carbon that was C=O now bears one H (from the original aldehyde), one R (the new ethyl from the Grignard), and one R' (the original chain). Aldehyde + Grignard always gives a secondary alcohol; ketones give tertiary; formaldehyde is the only carbonyl that gives a primary.

items.stem: Two molecules of acetone are mixed with a catalytic amount of NaOH in water at 30 degC and the mixture is warmed to drive off water. Which product set best describes this base-catalyzed aldol condensation?
choices: Diacetone alcohol (beta-hydroxy ketone), dehydrating to mesityl oxide on heating
items.why: Catalytic base creates an acetone enolate that attacks a second acetone carbonyl, forming the beta-hydroxy ketone diacetone alcohol. Heat then drives E1cb elimination of water to give the alpha,beta-unsaturated enone mesityl oxide. This is the classic acetone aldol-then-condensation sequence (addition first, dehydration on heating).

items.stem: 2-Butanone is treated with 1.1 equivalents of methylmagnesium bromide (MeMgBr) in dry THF at 0 degC, followed by aqueous workup. Methyl carbanion adds to the carbonyl carbon, generating an alkoxide that is protonated. What functional group results?
items.why: Grignard addition to a ketone gives a tertiary alcohol because the original carbonyl carbon already bore two R groups, and the Grignard adds a third. So 2-butanone (CH3COCH2CH3) plus MeMgBr puts a new methyl on the carbonyl carbon, giving 2-methyl-2-butanol, a tertiary alcohol.

items.stem: Butanal is treated with 1.1 equivalents of CH3MgBr in dry diethyl ether at 0 degC, then quenched with saturated aqueous NH4Cl. What functional group is present in the major product?
items.why: Grignard addition to an aldehyde always gives a secondary alcohol: the former carbonyl carbon ends up with one H (from the aldehyde), the new alkyl group (from the Grignard), and the rest of the parent chain. Butanal + MeMgBr therefore gives 2-pentanol, a secondary alcohol.

items.stem: Acetaldehyde is treated with 1.0 equivalent of phenylmagnesium bromide (PhMgBr) in dry THF at 0 degC, followed by aqueous NH4Cl workup. The Grignard delivers a phenyl carbanion to the carbonyl carbon. What functional group results?
items.why: Phenyl carbanion (from PhMgBr) is just another carbon nucleophile, so the rule still applies: aldehyde + Grignard gives a secondary alcohol. Acetaldehyde (CH3CHO) plus PhMgBr installs a phenyl on the carbonyl carbon, giving 1-phenylethanol (a secondary alcohol with H, methyl, and phenyl on the new sp3 carbon).

items.stem: An aldehyde is heated with 2 equivalents of ethanol and a catalytic amount of p-TsOH in dry toluene, with water removed by a Dean-Stark trap to drive the equilibrium forward. What is the functional class of the major product?
items.why: The acetal-formation equilibrium (aldehyde + 2 ROH = acetal + H2O) is normally unfavorable, but a Dean-Stark trap continuously removes water, pushing the equilibrium toward the acetal by Le Chatelier's principle. Two ethoxy groups end up on the original carbonyl carbon, giving R-CH(OEt)2.

items.stem: Benzaldehyde is treated with 1.1 equivalents of methylmagnesium bromide in dry THF at 0 degC, then quenched with aqueous NH4Cl. Methyl carbanion adds to the C=O of an aldehyde. What functional group is present in the product?
items.why: Grignard addition to an aldehyde gives a secondary alcohol because the new sp3 carbon bears H (from the aldehyde), a new alkyl group (from the Grignard), and the rest of the parent (here, phenyl). Benzaldehyde plus MeMgBr gives 1-phenylethanol, a secondary alcohol.

items.stem: Two molecules of acetone are combined with a catalytic amount of dilute NaOH in water and warmed gently. After the initial aldol addition, the mixture is heated to drive off water. Which sequence describes the products?
choices: Diacetone alcohol (beta-hydroxy ketone), which dehydrates to mesityl oxide on heating
items.why: Aldol addition: NaOH deprotonates one acetone alpha-CH to give an enolate, which attacks a second acetone's carbonyl, giving diacetone alcohol (a beta-hydroxy ketone). On heating, E1cb dehydration eliminates water to give the conjugated enone mesityl oxide. Claisen condensation requires esters (not ketones) and would give a beta-ketoester, not a beta-hydroxy ketone.

items.stem: Cyclohexanone is treated with 1.0 equivalent of LiAlH4 in dry THF at 0 degC, followed by careful aqueous workup. Hydride is delivered to the carbonyl carbon, generating an alkoxide that is protonated on workup. What is the product?
items.why: LiAlH4 reduces the C=O of a ketone to a C-OH; the new sp3 carbon bears one H (from hydride) and two carbons (the ring atoms), making it a secondary alcohol. Cyclohexanone is reduced to cyclohexanol, the textbook example of a hydride reduction of a cyclic ketone.

items.stem: Cyclohexanone is treated with 1.1 equivalents of methylmagnesium bromide (MeMgBr) in dry diethyl ether at 0 degC, then quenched with saturated aqueous NH4Cl. The methyl carbanion adds to the ketone C=O. What functional group results?
items.why: A Grignard addition to a ketone always gives a tertiary alcohol: the original carbonyl carbon already had two carbon substituents (here, both ring carbons), and the Grignard adds a third (methyl). The product, 1-methylcyclohexanol, has three carbons and one OH on the same sp3 carbon.

items.stem: Two equivalents of acetone are combined under a catalytic amount of NaOH at 25 degC, then heated to 60 degC. The base generates an enolate that attacks a second acetone, after which heat eliminates water from the beta-hydroxy ketone. Which sequence is correct?
choices: Diacetone alcohol (beta-hydroxy ketone), then mesityl oxide after dehydration
A methyl ester via Claisen condensation
items.why: The classic NaOH-catalyzed aldol of acetone proceeds in two stages: first, enolate addition gives diacetone alcohol (a beta-hydroxy ketone). On warming, E1cb dehydration removes the beta-OH and an alpha-H to give the conjugated alpha,beta-unsaturated ketone mesityl oxide. Conjugation with the carbonyl is the thermodynamic driving force for dehydration.

items.stem: Acetaldehyde (CH3CHO) is treated with 1.1 equivalents of n-butylmagnesium bromide in dry THF at -10 degC, followed by aqueous NH4Cl workup. The Grignard delivers an n-butyl carbanion once to the C=O. What is the functional class of the product?
items.why: Grignard addition to any aldehyde other than formaldehyde gives a secondary alcohol: the new sp3 carbon has one H (from the aldehyde), one R from the original aldehyde chain, and one R from the Grignard. Acetaldehyde + n-BuMgBr gives 2-hexanol, a secondary alcohol.

items.stem: Propanal is treated with 1.1 equivalents of methylmagnesium bromide (MeMgBr) in dry THF at 0 degC, then quenched with saturated aqueous NH4Cl. Methyl carbanion adds once to the aldehyde C=O. What is the functional class of the product?
items.why: Aldehyde + Grignard gives a secondary alcohol because the new sp3 carbon bears one H (from the aldehyde) plus two carbons (the original aldehyde chain and the new Grignard alkyl). Propanal (CH3CH2CHO) + MeMgBr gives 2-butanol, a secondary alcohol with one H and two carbon substituents.

items.stem: Two equivalents of acetone are stirred with a catalytic amount of dilute aqueous NaOH at 30 degC and then warmed to drive off water. Which products best describe the base-catalyzed aldol condensation that follows?
choices: Diacetone alcohol, then mesityl oxide on warming
An imine of acetone, formed by condensation at the carbonyl
Methyl acetate, formed via a Claisen condensation
Acetic acid, formed via haloform oxidation of acetone
Acetone cyanohydrin, formed by addition at C=O
items.why: An aldol condensation is two stages: (1) addition - enolate attacks a second carbonyl giving a beta-hydroxy ketone (diacetone alcohol from acetone), and (2) dehydration - heat triggers E1cb loss of water to give the conjugated alpha,beta-unsaturated enone (mesityl oxide). Conjugation provides the thermodynamic driving force for dehydration.

items.stem: Hexanal is treated with 1.1 equivalents of phenylmagnesium bromide (PhMgBr) in dry THF at 0 degC, followed by aqueous NH4Cl workup. The phenyl carbanion adds to the aldehyde C=O once. What is the functional class of the product?
items.why: Grignard + aldehyde gives a secondary alcohol because the new sp3 carbon ends up with one H (from the aldehyde), the original alkyl chain, and the new aryl/alkyl group from the Grignard. Hexanal + PhMgBr gives 1-phenyl-1-hexanol, a benzylic secondary alcohol.

items.stem: Acetone is treated with 1.1 equivalents of phenylmagnesium bromide in dry THF at 0 degC, then quenched with aqueous NH4Cl. The phenyl carbanion adds to the ketone carbonyl carbon, which is flanked by two carbon substituents and the new phenyl group. What functional class results?
items.why: Grignard + ketone always gives a tertiary alcohol because the original carbonyl carbon already has two carbon substituents (the two methyls of acetone), and the Grignard adds a third (phenyl). The product, 2-phenyl-2-propanol, has three carbon groups (two methyls and a phenyl) plus an OH on the same sp3 carbon.

items.stem: Propanal is treated with 2 equivalents of ethanol and a catalytic amount of TsOH in dry toluene, with continuous removal of water by molecular sieves to push the equilibrium forward. What functional class describes the major product?
choices: Acetal (two OR groups on the original carbonyl carbon)
Hemiacetal (one OR and one OH on the same carbon)
items.why: Aldehyde + 2 ROH under acid catalysis is an equilibrium that gives water and an acetal (R-CH(OR')2). The acetal is normally not the favored species in equilibrium, but molecular sieves trap the byproduct water, forcing the equilibrium toward acetal by Le Chatelier's principle. Propanal + EtOH thus gives the diethyl acetal.

items.stem: Benzaldehyde is heated with 2 equivalents of ethanol and a catalytic amount of p-TsOH in dry benzene, with water removed by a Dean-Stark trap. The protonated carbonyl is attacked by ethanol to give a hemiacetal, which is converted to the next stable species. Which functional class is the final product?
choices: Hemiacetal (the reaction stops here without water removal)
Acetal (two OR groups on the original carbonyl carbon)
items.why: The mechanism: ethanol adds to the protonated benzaldehyde to give a hemiacetal, the OH is protonated and leaves as water (driven off by the Dean-Stark trap), an oxocarbenium ion forms, and a second ethanol adds to give the acetal R-CH(OEt)2. Without removing water, the equilibrium would stop at hemiacetal (or revert); the Dean-Stark trap is what pushes it to the acetal.

items.stem: Carboxylic acids (pKa ~ 4-5) are dramatically more acidic than alcohols (pKa ~ 16-17). Which factor most directly accounts for this approximately 10^12 difference in Ka?
choices: Inductive (sigma) electron withdrawal of the C=O alone
The conjugate base (carboxylate, RCOO-) is resonance-stabilized over two equivalent oxygens
The O-H bond of a carboxylic acid is stronger than that of an alcohol
The alpha C-H bond is unusually weak
Carboxylic acids form intramolecular hydrogen bonds in the protonated state
items.why: Acidity is governed by conjugate-base stability. The carboxylate (RCOO-) delocalizes its negative charge equally over two oxygens by resonance, while an alkoxide (RO-) has its charge localized on a single oxygen. That added stabilization (two equivalent resonance structures with full octets) is worth about 10^12 in Ka. Inductive withdrawal helps but is much smaller than the resonance term.

items.stem: Methyl propanoate is heated with 1 equivalent of aqueous NaOH at reflux (saponification). Hydroxide attacks the carbonyl, the tetrahedral intermediate collapses, and an alkoxide leaves. After workup, what are the products?
choices: A carboxylate salt (RCOO- Na+) + an alcohol
items.why: Saponification (base-mediated ester hydrolysis) is irreversible because the final acid-base step deprotonates the carboxylic acid and traps the carboxylate salt, removing it from equilibrium. The overall result is the carboxylate (RCOO- Na+) plus the alcohol (here methanol). Acidic workup would protonate the carboxylate to give the free carboxylic acid.

items.stem: Acetic acid (pKa 4.76) is over 10 orders of magnitude more acidic than ethanol (pKa 15.9). What is the dominant electronic reason for this large difference?
choices: The alpha C-H bond is unusually weak
The conjugate base (carboxylate) is stabilized by resonance delocalization onto a second oxygen
The carboxylic O-H bond is stronger than the alcohol O-H bond
Pure inductive withdrawal by C=O without resonance
items.why: Acidity reflects conjugate base stability. The carboxylate has two equivalent resonance structures placing negative charge on either oxygen, so the charge is fully delocalized; an alkoxide has all the charge on one oxygen. That resonance stabilization is the dominant factor (worth ~10^11 in Ka), with inductive withdrawal a smaller secondary contributor.

items.stem: Acetyl chloride is treated with 2 equivalents of methylamine (CH3NH2) in dry CH2Cl2 at 0 degC. The amine attacks the carbonyl carbon, chloride leaves, and a second equivalent of amine deprotonates the ammonium intermediate. What are the products?
choices: An amide + HCl (trapped as the methylammonium chloride)
items.why: Acid chlorides are the most reactive acid derivative because Cl- is the best leaving group. The amine attacks the carbonyl, Cl- leaves, and the second equivalent of amine deprotonates the ammonium intermediate, giving an amide; that's why two equivalents are needed (one to react, one to neutralize HCl). The byproduct is methylammonium chloride (CH3NH3+ Cl-).

items.stem: Propanoic acid is heated with excess ethanol and a catalytic amount of concentrated H2SO4 at reflux for several hours. What is the name of this reaction and what are the products?
choices: Saponification, giving a carboxylate salt and an alcohol
Acidic hydrolysis, giving a carboxylic acid and an alcohol
Aldol addition, giving a beta-hydroxy ester product
Fischer esterification, giving ethyl propanoate and water
Claisen condensation, giving a beta-keto ester
items.why: Carboxylic acid + alcohol with H+ catalyst at reflux is the classic Fischer esterification: H+ activates the carbonyl, the alcohol attacks, and a tetrahedral intermediate collapses with loss of water. Excess alcohol pushes the reversible equilibrium forward (Le Chatelier). The products are the corresponding ester (ethyl propanoate) and water.

items.stem: Carboxylic acid derivatives differ in reactivity toward nucleophilic acyl substitution based on the leaving group ability and resonance donation of the heteroatom. Which ranking of acid derivatives is correct, from most to least reactive?
items.why: Reactivity in nucleophilic acyl substitution tracks leaving group ability and inverse pi donation: acid chlorides have the best leaving group (Cl-) and the worst pi donation (most electrophilic carbonyl), so they're most reactive; amides have the worst leaving group (NR2-) and the strongest pi donation (least electrophilic), so they're least reactive. The full order is acid chloride > anhydride > ester > amide.

items.stem: Ethyl acetate is heated at reflux with 1.0 equivalent of aqueous NaOH for 2 hours. Hydroxide attacks the ester carbonyl in an irreversible saponification to give a tetrahedral intermediate that collapses with loss of ethoxide. What are the final isolated products?
choices: A sodium carboxylate (RCOO- Na+) + an alcohol
items.why: Saponification is irreversible because the final step deprotonates the carboxylic acid to give the carboxylate salt, which is much more stable than reprotonation back to acid plus ethoxide. So ethyl acetate + NaOH gives sodium acetate (CH3COO- Na+) plus ethanol; acidic workup would convert the carboxylate to the free carboxylic acid (acetic acid).

items.stem: Acetyl chloride (CH3COCl) is treated with two equivalents of methylamine (CH3NH2) in anhydrous dichloromethane at 0 degrees C. After workup, what are the principal organic and inorganic products of this nucleophilic acyl substitution?
choices: N-methylacetamide and HCl (trapped as methylammonium chloride)
items.why: Acid chlorides are the most reactive carboxylic acid derivatives because Cl- is an excellent leaving group. The amine attacks the carbonyl carbon, the tetrahedral intermediate collapses to expel chloride, and a second equivalent of amine deprotonates the nitrogen, giving the amide and HCl (trapped by excess amine).

items.stem: Considering the leaving-group ability and resonance donation of the heteroatom attached to the carbonyl carbon, rank the following carboxylic acid derivatives from MOST reactive to LEAST reactive toward nucleophilic acyl substitution: amide, ester, anhydride, acid chloride.
items.why: Reactivity correlates inversely with resonance donation from the heteroatom into the carbonyl. Cl donates poorly (weakest pi overlap, best leaving group), making acid chlorides most reactive. Amide nitrogen donates strongly into the carbonyl, stabilizing it and making amides least reactive.

items.stem: Methyl benzoate is heated with aqueous NaOH (1.1 equiv) in ethanol/water at reflux for 4 hours. After cooling, what are the immediate organic products of this saponification, prior to any acidic workup?
items.why: Saponification is base-promoted ester hydrolysis. Hydroxide attacks the carbonyl, the tetrahedral intermediate expels methoxide, and the carboxylic acid is rapidly deprotonated by base to give the carboxylate salt. The reaction is irreversible because of this final deprotonation step.

items.stem: Acetic acid is refluxed with excess ethanol in the presence of catalytic concentrated H2SO4 with a Dean-Stark trap to remove water. Identify the reaction name and the principal organic product formed under these conditions.
choices: Fischer esterification giving ethyl acetate plus water
Saponification giving sodium acetate and ethanol
Aldol condensation giving a beta-hydroxy ester
Acid-catalyzed hydrolysis giving acetic acid and ethanol
items.why: Fischer esterification is the H+-catalyzed condensation of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol, forming an ester and water through a PADPED mechanism. The Dean-Stark trap removes water to push the equilibrium toward the ester product per Le Chatelier.

items.stem: Propanoic acid is combined with isopropanol and a catalytic amount of p-toluenesulfonic acid, then heated at reflux in toluene with azeotropic removal of water. Name the reaction and identify the principal organic product.
choices: Aldol addition giving a beta-hydroxy ester
Acid hydrolysis giving propanoic acid and isopropanol
Fischer esterification giving isopropyl propanoate plus water
items.why: Under acid catalysis, the carboxylic acid undergoes nucleophilic acyl substitution by the alcohol (PADPED mechanism), losing water to form an ester. Removing water by azeotropic distillation drives the equilibrium toward the ester.

items.stem: Ethyl butanoate is treated with 1.0 M aqueous NaOH at 80 degrees C for 3 hours, followed by aqueous workup without acidification. Identify the predominant species present in the aqueous phase.
items.why: Saponification proceeds via hydroxide addition to the ester carbonyl and loss of ethoxide. The carboxylic acid intermediate is immediately deprotonated by hydroxide to give the carboxylate, making the reaction irreversible. Without an acidic workup, the product remains as the sodium salt.

items.stem: A medicinal chemist must rank acyl-transfer reactivity to choose a coupling reagent. Considering pi-donation from the heteroatom and leaving-group ability, place these derivatives in order of decreasing reactivity toward a generic nucleophile: ester, amide, anhydride, acid chloride.
items.why: The reactivity order tracks resonance donation: chlorine (poor pi-donor, best LG) gives the most electrophilic carbonyl, while nitrogen (strong pi-donor) deactivates the amide carbonyl most. Anhydrides sit between acid chlorides and esters because the second acyl group is mildly stabilizing.

items.stem: Considering the relative pKa of the conjugate acid of each leaving group and the extent of resonance donation into the carbonyl, which ordering correctly ranks carboxylic acid derivatives from most reactive to least reactive in nucleophilic acyl substitution?
items.why: Better leaving groups (lower pKa of conjugate acid: HCl ~ -7, RCO2H ~ 5, ROH ~ 16, R2NH ~ 35) and weaker pi-donation give a more electrophilic carbonyl. The standard hierarchy is acid chloride > anhydride > ester > amide.

items.stem: Benzoyl chloride is added dropwise to a stirred solution of diethylamine (2.2 equiv) in anhydrous tetrahydrofuran at 0 degrees C. After warming to room temperature, what are the principal organic and inorganic products?
choices: N,N-Diethylbenzamide and the amine HCl salt
items.why: Acid chlorides react rapidly with secondary amines to give tertiary amides via nucleophilic acyl substitution. The first equivalent of amine forms the tetrahedral intermediate that loses chloride; the second equivalent acts as a base, neutralizing HCl as the alkylammonium salt.

items.stem: A graduate student designs a one-pot acylation cascade and must select the most reactive acyl donor for the first transfer step, then plan downstream conversion to the least reactive derivative. Rank these from most to least reactive: amide, ester, anhydride, acid chloride.
items.why: Acid chlorides are the most electrophilic because Cl is a weak pi-donor and excellent leaving group. Amides are least reactive because the lone pair on nitrogen donates strongly into the carbonyl. Synthetically, you typically descend the ladder (acyl chloride to anhydride to ester to amide) but cannot ascend without activation.

items.stem: Consider the relative free-energy barriers for nucleophilic addition to each acyl carbonyl and the energetics of leaving-group departure. Which sequence correctly orders carboxylic acid derivatives from MOST to LEAST reactive in nucleophilic acyl substitution?
items.why: Reactivity is governed by carbonyl electrophilicity (less pi-donation from the leaving group) and leaving-group stability (lower pKa of its conjugate acid). Both factors favor acid chlorides most and amides least, with anhydrides and esters in between.

items.stem: (2-Bromobutyl)trimethylammonium hydroxide is heated at 150 degrees C, conditions characteristic of Hofmann elimination. Which combination of reagent characteristics and product regiochemistry correctly describes a Hofmann elimination?
choices: Strong, bulky base (e.g., quaternary ammonium hydroxide on heating) gives the less-substituted (Hofmann) alkene
Heat alone gives the more-substituted (Zaitsev) alkene
Acidic conditions with H2SO4 give the Zaitsev product
SN2 conditions with hydroxide give the substitution product preferentially
Photolysis gives a radical-mediated Markovnikov alkene
items.why: Hofmann elimination uses a bulky leaving group and effectively bulky base, so steric strain in the transition state forces the base to remove the most accessible (least-hindered) beta-hydrogen. The result is the less-substituted (terminal) alkene, opposite of Zaitsev.

items.stem: Aqueous pKaH values for ammonia, methylamine, dimethylamine, and trimethylamine are roughly 9.3, 10.6, 10.8, and 9.8. Based on these values, which ranking best describes the basicity of NH3 versus 1, 2, and 3 degrees aliphatic amines in water?
choices: 3 deg > 2 deg > 1 deg > NH3 in all phases
2 deg > 1 deg approx 3 deg > NH3 in water; gas-phase order is 3 deg > 2 deg > 1 deg
All four are equally basic because nitrogen always has one lone pair
1 deg > 2 deg > 3 deg > NH3 in both water and gas phase
items.why: In the gas phase, alkyl groups donate inductively, giving 3 deg > 2 deg > 1 deg > NH3. In water, the trend is offset by hydrogen-bond solvation of the protonated amine: more N-H bonds give better solvation of the conjugate acid. The two effects combine to give 2 deg > 1 deg approx 3 deg > NH3.

items.stem: Acetone is treated with one equivalent of methylamine in methanol with NaBH3CN as the reducing agent and a trace of acetic acid to maintain pH approximately 5-6. What is the principal organic product after workup?
choices: Acetonitrile from dehydration of the iminium
2-Propanol from carbonyl reduction without C-N bond formation
items.why: Reductive amination forms an iminium ion (R2C=NHR+) from ketone + amine under mild acid catalysis; NaBH3CN selectively reduces the iminium without reducing the parent ketone, giving a secondary amine. The mild acidity enables iminium formation while keeping NaBH3CN active.

items.stem: Aqueous-phase pKaH measurements give ammonia approximately 9.3, methylamine 10.6, dimethylamine 10.8, and trimethylamine 9.8. Based on these values, which sequence correctly orders aqueous basicity of NH3, primary, secondary, and tertiary aliphatic amines?
choices: 2 deg > 1 deg approx 3 deg > NH3 in water; gas-phase order is 3 deg > 2 deg > 1 deg
3 deg > 2 deg > 1 deg > NH3 regardless of phase
1 deg > NH3 > 2 deg > 3 deg in water
items.why: In water, basicity reflects two competing effects: alkyl induction stabilizes the cation (favoring 3 deg) but loss of N-H bonds reduces solvation of the conjugate acid (disfavoring 3 deg). The competition gives 2 deg > 1 deg approx 3 deg > NH3, while the gas-phase order (no solvation) is 3 deg > 2 deg > 1 deg.

items.stem: Two effects govern aliphatic amine basicity in water: (i) inductive donation from alkyl groups stabilizes the ammonium cation; (ii) N-H bonds of the protonated amine hydrogen-bond with water to stabilize the conjugate acid. Based on these factors, what is the correct aqueous basicity order for NH3, 1, 2, and 3 deg aliphatic amines?
choices: All equivalent because N has one lone pair
3 deg > 2 deg > 1 deg > NH3 (gas-phase trend, regardless of solvent)
2 deg > 1 deg approx 3 deg > NH3 in water; gas-phase 3 deg > 2 deg > 1 deg
items.why: Inductive donation favors 3 deg amines, but solvation of the conjugate ammonium ion needs N-H bonds that 3 deg amines lack. In water the two effects roughly cancel for tertiary amines, giving 2 deg > 1 deg approx 3 deg > NH3, whereas the gas phase keeps the pure inductive ordering 3 deg > 2 deg > 1 deg.

items.stem: Acetone is mixed with methylamine (1.0 equiv) in methanol containing NaBH3CN and a catalytic amount of acetic acid (pH approximately 5). After 12 hours and aqueous workup, what is the major organic product of this reductive amination?
choices: The unreduced imine isolated as a yellow oil
N,N-dimethyl-2-propanamine (a tertiary amine from double alkylation)
items.why: Under mildly acidic conditions, the ketone and amine condense to an iminium ion that is selectively reduced by NaBH3CN. NaBH3CN is too weak a hydride donor to reduce the parent ketone but adequate for the more electrophilic iminium, cleanly giving the secondary amine.

items.stem: Acetone (1 equiv) and methylamine (1 equiv) are stirred in methanol with NaBH3CN as the reducing agent and acetic acid to buffer the medium near pH 5-6. After 8 h and aqueous workup, identify the major organic product.
choices: Acetonitrile, formed by elimination from the iminium
Isopropanol, formed by direct ketone reduction
items.why: Mild acid catalyzes condensation to the iminium, which NaBH3CN selectively reduces without touching the parent ketone. Combining a 1 deg amine with a ketone in this protocol stops cleanly at the secondary amine.

items.stem: Aniline (PhNH2, pKaH approximately 4.6) and methylamine (CH3NH2, pKaH approximately 10.6) are compared as Bronsted bases in water at 25 degrees C. How does the basicity of aniline compare to that of methylamine, and what is the structural reason?
choices: Aniline is less basic because the nitrogen lone pair is delocalized into the benzene ring
The two are essentially equally basic; both have one lone pair on nitrogen
Aniline is more basic because the phenyl group is electron-donating by induction
Comparison is impossible without solvent specification
Aniline is more basic because the protonated form is aromatic
items.why: In aniline, the nitrogen lone pair is conjugated into the aromatic pi system, lowering its availability and stabilizing the neutral amine relative to its protonated form. The result is a pKaH about 6 units lower than methylamine, making aniline roughly a million times less basic.

items.stem: An undergrad measures aqueous pKaH values: NH3 = 9.3, MeNH2 = 10.6, Me2NH = 10.8, Me3N = 9.8. Which generalization correctly captures the aqueous basicity ordering, with a note on the gas-phase trend?
choices: 2 deg > 1 deg approx 3 deg > NH3 in water; gas-phase 3 deg > 2 deg > 1 deg
All four are essentially equal because N is the basic atom
3 deg > 2 deg > 1 deg > NH3 in all conditions
1 deg > 2 deg > 3 deg > NH3 in water
items.why: Inductive donation from alkyls stabilizes the ammonium cation (favoring 3 deg). Hydrogen-bond solvation of the cation requires N-H bonds (favoring 1 deg/2 deg). In water these compete, giving 2 deg > 1 deg approx 3 deg > NH3; in gas phase only induction matters, giving 3 deg > 2 deg > 1 deg.

items.stem: When ranking the basicities of NH3, methylamine, dimethylamine, and trimethylamine in water, two opposing effects must be balanced: alkyl induction stabilizes the cation, while solvation of the cation requires N-H hydrogen-bond donors. What is the correct aqueous order?
choices: 2 deg > 1 deg approx 3 deg > NH3 in water; gas-phase 3 deg > 2 deg > 1 deg
items.why: Alkyl induction favors 3 deg amines, but solvation of the protonated amine needs N-H bonds to hydrogen-bond with water. The two effects roughly cancel for tertiary amines, leaving 2 deg > 1 deg approx 3 deg > NH3 in water; without solvation (gas phase), pure induction gives 3 deg > 2 deg > 1 deg.

items.stem: Aniline has pKaH approximately 4.6 in water, while methylamine has pKaH approximately 10.6. Considering hybridization, resonance, and inductive contributions to lone-pair availability, how does the basicity of aniline compare to methylamine?
choices: The two species cannot be compared because they have different hybridization at nitrogen
Aniline is far less basic, because the lone pair is delocalized into the aromatic ring and is therefore less available for protonation
Aniline is more basic, because the phenyl group donates electron density inductively
They are essentially equally basic, since both nitrogens are sp3
Aniline is more basic, because protonation generates an aromatic ammonium
items.why: Conjugation of the nitrogen lone pair with the benzene ring stabilizes the free amine and removes electron density from N. Protonation disrupts that conjugation and is therefore disfavored, lowering pKaH by about 6 units relative to methylamine.

items.stem: A 1:1 mixture of acetone and methylamine is stirred in methanol with NaBH3CN and a catalytic amount of glacial acetic acid (buffered around pH 5). After 12 hours and aqueous workup, which species predominates in the organic phase?
choices: Acetonitrile from over-reduction of the iminium
Isopropanol, from direct hydride reduction of the ketone
items.why: Mildly acidic buffer favors iminium formation, and NaBH3CN selectively reduces iminium ions over ketones at this pH. Stoichiometry (1:1 amine/ketone) terminates the alkylation at the secondary amine and avoids over-alkylation to the tertiary amine.

items.stem: Considering the competing effects of alkyl induction (favoring more substituted amines) and hydrogen-bond solvation of the conjugate acid (requiring N-H bonds), which sequence correctly orders the aqueous basicities of NH3 and the 1, 2, 3 deg aliphatic amines?
choices: All four approximately equal in water
items.why: Pure induction (gas phase) gives 3 deg > 2 deg > 1 deg > NH3, but hydrogen-bond stabilization of the protonated amine in water depends on N-H bonds, partially offsetting the induction trend. Net aqueous basicity is 2 deg > 1 deg approx 3 deg > NH3.

items.stem: Aqueous pKaH measurements give ammonia approximately 9.3, methylamine 10.6, dimethylamine 10.8, and trimethylamine 9.8. Considering both alkyl induction and hydrogen-bond solvation, which ordering best summarizes the relative basicity in water?
choices: 2 deg > 1 deg approx 3 deg > NH3 in water; gas-phase 3 deg > 2 deg > 1 deg
3 deg > 2 deg > 1 deg > NH3 in all conditions
items.why: Alkyl groups stabilize the protonated amine inductively (favoring 3 deg), but hydrogen-bond solvation of the cation requires N-H bonds (favoring 1 deg/2 deg). In water, those effects compete, yielding 2 deg > 1 deg approx 3 deg > NH3.

items.stem: Computational studies confirm a gas-phase basicity order of 3 deg > 2 deg > 1 deg > NH3 (pure induction), but aqueous pKaH measurements give a different order. Considering both inductive donation and differential solvation of the alkylammonium cation, which sequence captures the experimental aqueous basicity?
choices: All four amines are essentially equivalent in water
3 deg > 2 deg > 1 deg > NH3 in water (matching gas-phase)
2 deg > 1 deg approx 3 deg > NH3 in water; gas-phase 3 deg > 2 deg > 1 deg
items.why: Solvation of an ammonium cation correlates with the number of N-H bonds available for hydrogen bonding to water. As alkyl substitution increases, induction strengthens but solvation weakens; the two effects compete to give 2 deg > 1 deg approx 3 deg > NH3 in water.

items.stem: Acetone and methylamine are combined in methanol with NaBH3CN and acetic acid buffer (pH approximately 5). After overnight stirring at room temperature, identify the major isolable amine product, recognizing that NaBH3CN is selective for iminium reduction at this pH.
choices: Acetonitrile, by elimination of the iminium
items.why: Acid catalysis condenses the amine and ketone into an iminium that is rapidly reduced by NaBH3CN, while the parent ketone is largely unaffected at this pH. Stoichiometric amine plus a primary amine partner cleanly stops at the secondary amine.

items.stem: A hydrocarbon with molecular formula CxHy is analyzed and the chemist must compute its degrees of unsaturation (rings plus pi bonds) before interpreting NMR data. Which formula correctly gives the degrees of unsaturation for a saturated reference of CnH2n+2?
items.why: Each ring or pi bond removes two hydrogens from the saturated parent CnH2n+2. Subtracting the observed H count from the saturated value and dividing by 2 yields the degrees of unsaturation, captured by (2x + 2 - y) / 2 for CxHy.

items.stem: A combustion analysis returns the empirical formula CxHy for a pure hydrocarbon. To plan its NMR interpretation, the analyst first needs the degrees of unsaturation. Which expression yields the correct number of rings plus pi bonds?
choices: Just count rings on the structure
items.why: Starting from the saturated formula CnH2n+2, every ring or pi bond eliminates two hydrogens. The general expression (2x + 2 - y) / 2 gives the count of rings plus pi bonds for a hydrocarbon CxHy.

items.stem: An unknown aromatic compound is analyzed by 1H NMR in CDCl3 referenced to TMS. In what chemical-shift range do typical aromatic ring protons (e.g., those of toluene or benzaldehyde) appear?
items.why: Aromatic protons sit in the deshielded region created by the ring current of the aromatic pi system. The induced magnetic field at the proton position adds to B0, pushing the resonance downfield to roughly 6.5 - 8.5 ppm.

items.stem: A student records the 1H NMR spectrum of a benzene derivative in CDCl3 and must identify the aromatic-proton region for integration. Which chemical-shift range is most characteristic of aromatic ring protons?
items.why: Aromatic ring protons are deshielded by the diamagnetic ring current generated when the ring is placed in B0. This effect places typical aromatic 1H signals in the 6.5 - 8.5 ppm window relative to TMS.

items.stem: After elemental analysis, a hydrocarbon is given the formula CxHy. The chemist must compute degrees of unsaturation (rings plus pi bonds) before assigning structure from NMR. Which formula provides that calculation?
choices: Just count rings in any tentative structure
items.why: Each ring or pi bond reduces the H count by two relative to the saturated parent CnH2n+2. The standard expression (2x + 2 - y) / 2 reports rings plus pi bonds for any hydrocarbon CxHy.

items.stem: A neat-film IR spectrum of an unknown organic liquid shows a broad, strong absorption spanning approximately 3200 - 3550 cm^-1, with no other notable feature in the 1700 cm^-1 region. Which functional group is most consistent with that signal?
choices: C identical N of a nitrile
items.why: Alcohol O-H stretches give a broad, strong absorption in the 3200 - 3550 cm^-1 region because intermolecular hydrogen bonding produces a wide distribution of bond strengths. C-H stretches appear near 2900 cm^-1, and amine N-H bands are usually narrower and lower-intensity than alcohol O-H.

items.stem: A 13C NMR spectrum of an unknown ester in CDCl3 is recorded with TMS internal reference. In which chemical-shift range does the carbonyl carbon of typical aldehydes, ketones, and esters generally appear?
items.why: Carbonyl carbons are heavily deshielded because of pi-bond electron withdrawal and sp2 hybridization, placing them around 160 - 220 ppm. Esters and acids fall closer to 165 - 175 ppm; aldehydes and ketones fall closer to 190 - 220 ppm.

items.stem: Combustion data give a hydrocarbon the formula CxHy, and the chemist needs the degrees of unsaturation to constrain its structure before NMR assignment. Which expression returns the correct rings-plus-pi count?
choices: Just visually count rings on a candidate structure
items.why: Each ring or pi bond costs two hydrogens relative to the saturated parent CnH2n+2. The expression (2x + 2 - y) / 2 captures that loss exactly for any pure hydrocarbon CxHy.

items.stem: A neat-film IR spectrum of an unknown shows a sharp, strong absorption near 1715 cm^-1 with no broad O-H feature above 3000 cm^-1 and no aldehydic C-H near 2720 cm^-1. Which functional group best explains the 1715 cm^-1 band?
choices: C identical C of an alkyne
items.why: Saturated ketone C=O stretches absorb near 1715 cm^-1 with strong, sharp character. The absence of a broad O-H band rules out an acid, and the lack of the aldehydic C-H 'doublet' near 2720/2820 cm^-1 rules out an aldehyde, leaving a ketone.

items.stem: An IR spectrum (neat liquid film, NaCl plates) shows a sharp, strong band at approximately 1715 cm^-1 with no broad absorption from 2500 - 3300 cm^-1 and no diagnostic aldehydic C-H near 2720 cm^-1. Identify the functional group responsible.
choices: C identical C of a terminal alkyne
items.why: Saturated ketones absorb near 1715 cm^-1, sharp and strong. The lack of a broad acidic O-H envelope rules out a carboxylic acid, and the missing aldehyde C-H stretch eliminates an aldehyde, indicating a ketone.

items.stem: An IR spectrum of an unknown organic compound shows a broad, strong absorption from approximately 3200 to 3550 cm^-1, no carbonyl stretch near 1715 cm^-1, and standard sp3 C-H bands near 2900 cm^-1. Which functional group is most consistent with the broad absorption?
items.why: Alcohol O-H stretches give a wide, strong absorption in the 3200 - 3550 cm^-1 window because of intermolecular hydrogen bonding. Without a carbonyl stretch, a carboxylic acid is excluded; the breadth and position rule out C-H, C-N, and C=C.

items.stem: A 1H NMR spectrum of an unknown shows a 3H triplet at 1.2 ppm coupled to a 2H quartet at 4.1 ppm (J approximately 7 Hz). Combined with an IR carbonyl stretch at 1735 cm^-1, what structural fragment does the triplet/quartet pair most likely indicate?
choices: An ethyl group (-CH2CH3) attached to a deshielding heteroatom
items.why: An ethyl group attached to oxygen (or another deshielding heteroatom) shows the textbook 3H triplet (CH3 split by 2 H) coupled to a 2H quartet (CH2 split by 3 H). The 4.1 ppm shift of the CH2 indicates attachment to an electronegative group such as -OC(=O)R.

items.stem: A 1H NMR spectrum displays a 3H triplet at 1.2 ppm coupled to a 2H quartet at approximately 3.5 ppm (J approximately 7 Hz). Considering n+1 multiplicity rules, which structural fragment is most consistent with this pattern?
choices: Aromatic protons of a phenyl group
An ethyl group (-CH2CH3) attached to a deshielding heteroatom
items.why: An ethyl group adjacent to an electronegative heteroatom gives a 3H triplet (CH3 coupling to two CH2 protons) and a 2H quartet (CH2 coupling to three CH3 protons). The downfield CH2 chemical shift confirms the attachment to a heteroatom such as oxygen or halogen.

items.stem: An IR spectrum (neat liquid film) shows a sharp, strong absorption at 1715 cm^-1 with no broad O-H stretch above 2500 cm^-1 and no diagnostic aldehyde C-H 'doublet' near 2720 cm^-1. Which functional group is responsible?
choices: C identical C of an alkyne
items.why: Saturated ketones absorb near 1715 cm^-1 (sharp, strong). The absence of a broad O-H band rules out a carboxylic acid, and the absence of the aldehyde C-H stretch around 2720 cm^-1 rules out an aldehyde.

items.stem: An aromatic compound is examined by 1H NMR in CDCl3 referenced to TMS. The aromatic ring's diamagnetic ring current pushes attached protons into a characteristic chemical-shift window. What range typically applies to aromatic ring protons?
items.why: Aromatic ring currents create a deshielding cone at the periphery of the ring, augmenting B0 at the proton positions. As a result, aromatic 1H signals appear deshielded relative to alkenyl protons, in the 6.5 - 8.5 ppm range.

items.stem: A student is reviewing chemical-shift tables for 1H NMR. Aromatic ring protons are deshielded relative to typical sp3 C-H protons because of the ring current induced by the aromatic pi system. What chemical-shift range is most characteristic for aromatic protons?
items.why: Aromatic ring currents produce a deshielding cone outside the ring plane, increasing the local field at attached protons. Typical aromatic 1H shifts thus fall in the 6.5 - 8.5 ppm window, downfield of vinyl and alkyl protons.

items.stem: An organic chemist is interpreting a 13C NMR spectrum of an unknown carbonyl compound dissolved in CDCl3. In which chemical-shift range do carbonyl carbons of aldehydes, ketones, esters, and acids generally appear?
items.why: Carbonyl carbons are sp2 hybridized and bonded to electronegative oxygen, leaving them strongly deshielded. The combined effects place their resonances at roughly 160 - 220 ppm, well downfield of aromatic and sp3 carbons.

items.stem: A 1H NMR spectrum of an unknown shows a 3H triplet at 1.25 ppm coupled to a 2H quartet at 4.10 ppm with J approximately 7 Hz. Combined with an IR carbonyl absorption at 1735 cm^-1, what structural fragment best explains the triplet/quartet pair?
choices: A methoxyl (-OCH3) of a methyl ester
An ethyl group (-CH2CH3) bound to a deshielding heteroatom (e.g., the ethyl ester -OCH2CH3)
An allyl methylene attached to a vinyl group
items.why: An ethyl ester O-CH2-CH3 gives the canonical 3H triplet/2H quartet pattern with J approximately 7 Hz. The 4.1 ppm CH2 shift indicates attachment to an electronegative oxygen, consistent with the ester carbonyl in the IR.

items.stem: A pure hydrocarbon of empirical formula CxHy is to be analyzed. Before assigning structure from NMR, the analyst must compute its degrees of unsaturation (rings plus pi bonds). Which formula correctly does so?
choices: Visually count rings on a guessed structure
items.why: Each ring or pi bond removes two hydrogens relative to the saturated parent CnH2n+2. The expression (2x + 2 - y) / 2 quantifies that loss for any pure hydrocarbon CxHy.

items.stem: An IR spectrum (neat film) of an unknown shows a sharp, strong absorption at 1715 cm^-1, no broad O-H envelope from 2500 - 3300 cm^-1, and no aldehydic C-H 'doublet' near 2720 cm^-1. Identify the functional group consistent with the 1715 cm^-1 band.
choices: C identical C of an alkyne
items.why: Saturated ketones absorb near 1715 cm^-1 (sharp, strong). The absence of a broad acidic O-H band excludes a carboxylic acid; the absence of the diagnostic aldehyde C-H stretch around 2720 cm^-1 excludes an aldehyde, leaving a ketone.

items.stem: A neat-liquid IR spectrum displays a sharp, strong absorption at 1715 cm^-1 with no broad O-H from 2500 - 3300 cm^-1 and no aldehydic C-H stretch near 2720 cm^-1. Considering frequency, intensity, and bandshape, which functional group best fits the 1715 cm^-1 band?
choices: C identical C of a terminal alkyne
items.why: Saturated ketones display a sharp, strong C=O stretch close to 1715 cm^-1. The absence of broad O-H or aldehyde C-H bands excludes the acid and aldehyde alternatives, leaving the ketone.

items.stem: A neat-liquid IR spectrum has a sharp, strong absorption at 1715 cm^-1, no broad O-H from 2500 - 3300 cm^-1, and no diagnostic aldehyde C-H stretch near 2720 cm^-1. Which functional group is most consistent with the 1715 cm^-1 absorption?
choices: C identical C of an alkyne
items.why: Saturated ketones absorb near 1715 cm^-1 (sharp, strong). The lack of broad O-H or aldehyde C-H stretches eliminates the carboxylic acid and aldehyde alternatives.

items.stem: Ethanol must be converted to ethyl chloride (chloroethane) cleanly without skeletal rearrangement, using the most reliable single-step method. Which reagent or reagent combination achieves this transformation?
choices: Thionyl chloride (SOCl2), or HCl with ZnCl2 (Lucas reagent)
Lithium aluminum hydride in dry ether
items.why: SOCl2 converts a primary alcohol to the alkyl chloride via a chlorosulfite intermediate, releasing SO2 and HCl as byproducts and avoiding the carbocation rearrangements that can plague HCl alone. Lucas reagent (HCl/ZnCl2) is an alternative that activates the alcohol toward chloride displacement.

items.stem: Ethene is to be converted into ethylene glycol (1,2-ethanediol) in a single step with syn-addition of two hydroxyl groups across the alkene. Which reagent system achieves a clean syn-dihydroxylation?
choices: HBr in the dark, polar protic solvent
Cold, dilute KMnO4 (or OsO4 / NMO) for syn-dihydroxylation
items.why: Cold, dilute aqueous KMnO4 (or OsO4 with a co-oxidant such as NMO) adds two hydroxyl groups syn across the alkene through a cyclic manganate or osmate ester intermediate. Hot KMnO4 over-oxidizes and cleaves the C=C, while H2/Pd reduces the alkene only.

items.stem: Acetylene (HC identical CH) must be converted to cis-2-butene in a multi-step sequence that installs both methyl groups and then sets the cis geometry. Which sequence accomplishes this?
choices: 1) NaNH2 then CH3I (twice, sequential alkylations); 2) H2 with Lindlar's catalyst
items.why: Sequential deprotonation of the terminal alkyne with NaNH2 followed by SN2 alkylation with CH3I builds the internal alkyne 2-butyne. Lindlar's catalyst (poisoned Pd) then performs syn-hydrogenation, delivering the cis-alkene specifically; Na/NH3 would give the trans isomer.

items.stem: A student needs to convert ethanol into ethyl chloride (chloroethane) with no carbocation rearrangement and minimal aqueous workup. Which reagent gives the cleanest one-step result on a primary alcohol?
items.why: SOCl2 transforms a 1 deg alcohol into the corresponding chloride via a chlorosulfite intermediate, releasing SO2 and HCl. Lucas reagent (HCl/ZnCl2) is the alternative for 2 deg/3 deg alcohols. PCC oxidizes; LiAlH4 reduces; NaOH does nothing useful here.

items.stem: Benzene is to be transformed into nitrobenzene by electrophilic aromatic substitution at 50 - 60 degrees C. Which reagent combination generates the nitronium electrophile and effects nitration?
items.why: Concentrated H2SO4 protonates HNO3 to generate the nitronium ion (NO2+), the active electrophile in benzene nitration. Aromatic addition followed by loss of H+ restores aromaticity and yields nitrobenzene; the other choices either halogenate, oxidize, or do not generate NO2+.

items.stem: Ethanol is to be converted to ethyl chloride (chloroethane) in a single, clean step that avoids carbocation rearrangement. Which reagent or reagent pair is preferred for this primary alcohol?
choices: Thionyl chloride (SOCl2), or HCl with ZnCl2 (Lucas reagent)
items.why: SOCl2 transforms a primary alcohol cleanly to its chloride via a chlorosulfite intermediate that loses SO2 with backside chloride attack. Lucas reagent (HCl/ZnCl2) is an effective alternative; PCC oxidizes, LiAlH4 reduces, and NaOH does not chlorinate.

items.stem: Benzene must be nitrated to give nitrobenzene at 50 - 60 degrees C by electrophilic aromatic substitution. Which reagent combination is required to generate the nitronium electrophile and accomplish nitration?
items.why: Concentrated H2SO4 activates HNO3 by protonation, generating NO2+ as the electrophile. Benzene attacks NO2+ to give a sigma-complex, which loses a proton to restore aromaticity, yielding nitrobenzene.

items.stem: Propanal (CH3CH2CHO) is to be reduced to 1-propanol selectively, leaving any ester or amide groups in the molecule untouched. Which reagent provides this selective carbonyl reduction?
items.why: NaBH4 is a mild hydride source that reduces aldehydes (and ketones) to alcohols but leaves esters, amides, and carboxylic acids essentially untouched. PCC and Jones oxidize; Br2 adds across double bonds; LiAlH4 (not listed) would over-reduce other groups.

items.stem: Ethene (CH2=CH2) is to be converted into ethylene glycol via syn-dihydroxylation, retaining both carbons of the alkene. Which reagent system achieves this transformation in one step?
choices: HBr in CH2Cl2 in the dark
Cold, dilute KMnO4 (or OsO4 / NMO) for syn-dihydroxylation
items.why: Cold, dilute KMnO4 (or OsO4 with NMO) forms a cyclic manganate or osmate ester that hydrolyzes to a syn-diol. Hot KMnO4 cleaves the C=C entirely, giving carboxylic acids or ketones, and is not suitable for diol synthesis.

items.stem: 1-Butyne is to be converted into 2-butanone (a methyl ketone) by Markovnikov hydration in a single step. Which reagent system accomplishes this regioselective alkyne hydration?
choices: BH3 in THF, then H2O2 / NaOH
H2O / H2SO4 with HgSO4 (Markovnikov hydration via enol tautomerization)
items.why: Mercuric-catalyzed acid hydration delivers water across a terminal alkyne with Markovnikov regiochemistry, generating an enol that tautomerizes to the methyl ketone (2-butanone). Hydroboration/oxidation would give the anti-Markovnikov product, butanal.

items.stem: 1-Bromopropane is to be converted into 1-propanol in one step via a SN2 process at the primary carbon, with no rearrangement. Which reagent provides the cleanest result?
items.why: Aqueous hydroxide is a strong nucleophile but not bulky, so it executes SN2 on a primary substrate cleanly to give 1-propanol. Sodium methoxide is also a good nucleophile but would give the methyl ether instead. PCC oxidizes alcohols; HCl would not displace bromide.

items.stem: Benzene must be nitrated to give nitrobenzene at 50 - 60 degrees C through electrophilic aromatic substitution. Which reagent combination generates the active electrophile (NO2+) and accomplishes the nitration?
items.why: Concentrated H2SO4 protonates HNO3 to generate NO2+, the electrophile. Benzene attacks NO2+, forming a Wheland sigma-complex that deprotonates to regenerate aromaticity, yielding nitrobenzene.

items.stem: Propanal is to be reduced selectively to 1-propanol while leaving any ester or carboxylic acid groups intact in the same molecule. Which reagent achieves this selective carbonyl reduction?
items.why: NaBH4 selectively delivers hydride to aldehydes and ketones, leaving esters and acids unchanged. Jones and PCC oxidize alcohols; Br2 brominates; H2SO4 dehydrates.

items.stem: 1-Butyne is to be hydrated regioselectively to form 2-butanone, the Markovnikov methyl ketone product. Which reagent system delivers water across the triple bond with Markovnikov regiochemistry?
choices: Aqueous H2SO4 with HgSO4 (Markovnikov hydration via enol tautomerization)
BH3 in THF, then H2O2 / NaOH
items.why: Mercury(II) catalysis delivers water across a terminal alkyne with Markovnikov regiochemistry. The intermediate enol tautomerizes to the methyl ketone (2-butanone). Hydroboration would give the aldehyde via anti-Markovnikov addition.

items.stem: Acetylene must be converted into cis-2-butene by a sequence that adds two methyl groups and sets the cis geometry across the resulting double bond. Which sequence accomplishes both objectives?
choices: LiAlH4 in dry ether, then Cl2/CCl4
1) NaNH2, then CH3I (sequential, twice). 2) H2 with Lindlar's catalyst
items.why: Two consecutive deprotonations of the terminal alkyne with NaNH2 and alkylations with CH3I install both methyl groups, giving 2-butyne. Lindlar's catalyst then syn-adds H2 to give cis-2-butene; Na/NH3 would deliver the trans isomer.

items.stem: A multi-step synthesis must convert acetylene to cis-2-butene by introducing both methyl groups and then setting the geometry of the resulting double bond. Which protocol achieves this exactly?
choices: 1) NaNH2, then CH3I (sequential alkylation, twice). 2) H2 with Lindlar's catalyst
items.why: Sequential NaNH2/CH3I alkylations build 2-butyne from acetylene. Lindlar's catalyst (poisoned Pd) then performs syn-addition of H2 to set the cis geometry; Na in liquid NH3 would generate the trans-alkene via radical anion intermediate.

items.stem: Ethanol is to be converted to ethyl chloride in one step, avoiding skeletal rearrangement and minimizing cleanup. Considering reagent compatibility with primary alcohols, which choice gives the cleanest result?
items.why: SOCl2 cleanly converts a primary alcohol to the chloride via a chlorosulfite intermediate, releasing only SO2 and HCl as byproducts. Lucas reagent (HCl/ZnCl2) is a useful alternative; the other listed reagents oxidize, reduce, or simply do not chlorinate.

items.stem: Acetylene is the starting material in a multi-step sequence that targets cis-2-butene. Which protocol installs both methyl groups and then delivers H2 with the cis geometry needed for the target alkene?
choices: 1) NaNH2, then CH3I (sequential, twice). 2) H2 with Lindlar's catalyst
LiAlH4 in dry ether, then Br2
items.why: Two sequential alkylations of the deprotonated acetylide with CH3I yield 2-butyne. Lindlar's catalyst then syn-adds H2 across the triple bond, giving the cis-alkene. Na/NH3 would give the trans isomer through dissolving-metal reduction.

items.stem: 1-Butyne is to be hydrated regioselectively in a single transformation to give 2-butanone, the Markovnikov methyl ketone. Which reagent system delivers water across the triple bond with the correct regiochemistry?
choices: BH3 in THF, then H2O2 / NaOH
H2O / H2SO4 with HgSO4 (Markovnikov hydration via enol tautomerization)
items.why: Mercury-catalyzed acid hydration of a terminal alkyne adds OH at the more substituted carbon, generating an enol that tautomerizes to the corresponding methyl ketone. Hydroboration/oxidation would instead give the anti-Markovnikov aldehyde, butanal.

items.stem: 1-Bromopropane is to be converted to 1-propanol by a single SN2 displacement at the primary carbon, avoiding any rearrangement or substitution at oxygen. Which reagent accomplishes this most cleanly?
choices: Aqueous NaOH (SN2 displacement of bromide by hydroxide)
items.why: Hydroxide is a strong nucleophile that executes a clean SN2 on primary halides, delivering 1-propanol. Methoxide would substitute to give the methyl ether instead. PCC oxidizes alcohols to carbonyls, and HCl would only re-protonate any alcohol formed.

items.stem: Ethene is to be converted into ethylene glycol by a single-step syn-dihydroxylation, with both hydroxyl groups added to the same face of the alkene. Which reagent system achieves this without C-C bond cleavage?
choices: Cold, dilute KMnO4 or OsO4 with NMO
items.why: Cold, dilute KMnO4 or OsO4 (with a co-oxidant such as NMO) creates a cyclic mangante or osmate ester that hydrolyzes to give the syn-1,2-diol. Hot KMnO4 over-oxidizes and cleaves the C=C; H2/Pd reduces only.

items.stem: 1-Butyne must be hydrated regioselectively to give 2-butanone (the Markovnikov methyl ketone) in one step. Which reagent system installs water with the necessary Markovnikov regiochemistry, including tautomerization of the enol to the ketone?
choices: BH3 in THF, then H2O2 / NaOH
H2O / H2SO4 with HgSO4 (Markovnikov hydration with enol tautomerization)
items.why: Mercury-catalyzed acid hydration of a terminal alkyne adds water with Markovnikov regiochemistry, giving an enol that tautomerizes to the methyl ketone (2-butanone). Hydroboration/oxidation would give the anti-Markovnikov aldehyde, butanal.

items.stem: An ether solution contains a neutral hydrocarbon and a small amount of a carboxylic acid impurity (pKa approximately 4-5). To selectively remove the acid into the aqueous layer without protonating any neutral organics, which aqueous wash should be used?
choices: Wash with 1 M HCl, which protonates any basic functional groups
Wash with saturated brine (NaCl) and discard the organic layer
Distill the entire mixture and collect the lower-boiling fraction
Wash with aqueous NaHCO3, which deprotonates only the acid
Wash with 1 M NaOH, which also deprotonates any phenols
items.why: Sodium bicarbonate (pKa of H2CO3 approximately 6.4) is basic enough to deprotonate carboxylic acids but not phenols (pKa approximately 10). Selective deprotonation converts only the acid to its water-soluble carboxylate, leaving the neutral hydrocarbon in the organic layer.

items.stem: A chemist needs to separate a complex mixture of small organic molecules whose primary differentiation is polarity. Which separation technique is best suited to resolve compounds based on differing polarity using a polar stationary phase?
choices: Column chromatography on silica with an organic eluent
items.why: Silica-gel column chromatography separates molecules by competitive adsorption: more polar analytes interact more strongly with the polar silica and elute later. By tuning eluent polarity, components are resolved on the basis of overall polarity differences.

items.stem: On a silica TLC plate developed in 30% EtOAc/hexanes, an analyte spot migrated 4.0 cm from the origin while the solvent front advanced 8.0 cm. Compute the retention factor (Rf) of the analyte.
items.why: Rf equals the distance traveled by the analyte divided by the distance traveled by the solvent front, both measured from the origin. Rf = 4.0 / 8.0 = 0.50.

items.stem: Two miscible liquids in a binary mixture have boiling points of 78 degrees C and 110 degrees C, respectively. Which laboratory technique is most appropriate for separating them based on the boiling-point difference?
choices: Distillation, simple or fractional, depending on the boiling-point gap
items.why: Distillation separates miscible liquids by exploiting differences in vapor pressure with temperature. With a boiling-point gap of approximately 30 degrees C, simple distillation is often sufficient; smaller gaps would require fractional distillation for better separation.

items.stem: A crude solid product contains a small amount of soluble impurity, and the desired compound is more soluble in hot solvent than cold. Which technique exploits this temperature-dependent solubility difference to purify the solid?
items.why: Recrystallization dissolves the crude solid in a minimum volume of hot solvent and slowly cools to crystallize the major component, leaving impurities in solution. The choice of solvent must give large solubility differences between hot and cold to be effective.

items.stem: A chemist wants to separate two miscible liquids whose boiling points differ by approximately 25 degrees C. Considering vapor-pressure differences and equipment requirements, which technique is best suited for this separation?
choices: Distillation, simple or fractional depending on the boiling-point gap
items.why: Distillation separates miscible liquids by their differing vapor pressures with temperature. A 25 degree gap is borderline for simple distillation; fractional distillation provides additional theoretical plates to ensure clean separation if simple distillation fails.

items.stem: Liquid-liquid extraction is used to separate a desired analyte between an aqueous phase and an organic phase like ether or DCM. Which physicochemical property is the basis for the separation?
choices: Crystal lattice energy of solid phases
Polarity of a stationary phase relative to a mobile phase
Differential solubility (partition coefficient) between two immiscible solvents
Difference in boiling point between solute and solvent
Differences in molar mass at constant temperature
items.why: Liquid-liquid extraction exploits the partition coefficient (Kd) of a solute between two immiscible solvents. Solutes preferring the less polar solvent partition into the organic layer; those preferring the polar solvent partition into water, often after acid-base manipulation.

items.stem: A solid product is contaminated with a more soluble impurity, and the desired compound shows a strongly temperature-dependent solubility. Which technique relies on this property to purify the major component without modifying it chemically?
items.why: Recrystallization dissolves the solid in a minimum volume of hot solvent and cools slowly. The pure compound crystallizes as the solubility decreases while the more soluble impurity remains in the mother liquor and is removed by filtration.

items.stem: After a small-scale synthesis, the solid product contains a soluble impurity, and the desired compound is much less soluble at low temperature than at high temperature. Which technique exploits these solubility differences to deliver a purer solid?
items.why: Recrystallization works by dissolving the crude solid at high temperature and slowly cooling to selectively crystallize the major component. Impurities that remain soluble in the cold mother liquor are removed during filtration.

items.stem: A student isolates a crystalline product from a Friedel-Crafts acylation that contains a small amount of soluble impurity. Considering temperature-dependent solubility, which technique is best for purifying the major solid compound?
items.why: Recrystallization exploits the increased solubility of the desired compound at high temperature and reduced solubility on cooling. Impurities present at low concentration remain dissolved in the mother liquor, while the major component crystallizes pure.

items.stem: An ether solution contains a neutral aromatic ester and a small carboxylic acid by-product (pKa approximately 4-5). To selectively transfer only the carboxylic acid into the aqueous layer without hydrolyzing the ester, which aqueous wash is preferred?
choices: Wash with saturated aqueous NaHCO3, which deprotonates the acid into a water-soluble carboxylate
Wash with 1 M NaOH (which would also saponify the ester)
items.why: Saturated NaHCO3 deprotonates carboxylic acids selectively (pKa 4-5) without being basic enough to hydrolyze esters. The water-soluble carboxylate moves into the aqueous layer; the neutral ester remains in the ether layer.

items.stem: A dichloromethane solution contains a neutral aromatic ester and a small carboxylic acid impurity. Considering pKa values and ester sensitivity to base, which aqueous wash will selectively remove only the acid into the aqueous phase?
choices: Wash with 1 M HCl, which protonates any basic groups present
Distill the entire mixture and discard the high-boiling residue
Wash with saturated brine (NaCl) and decant the organic layer
Wash with 1 M NaOH, which also hydrolyzes some of the ester
Wash with aqueous NaHCO3, which spares the ester
items.why: Bicarbonate (pKa of H2CO3 approximately 6.4) is basic enough to deprotonate carboxylic acids but too weak to deprotonate phenols (pKa approximately 10) or hydrolyze esters. The carboxylate ion enters the aqueous phase; the ester stays organic.

items.stem: A chemist must separate a mixture of structurally similar compounds that differ mainly in polarity. Which technique provides the highest resolution for analytical or preparative-scale separations based on polarity?
choices: Column chromatography on silica gel with an organic eluent
items.why: Silica-gel column chromatography separates compounds by competitive adsorption between a polar stationary phase and a less polar mobile phase. Tuning eluent polarity controls retention, allowing resolution of analytes with subtle polarity differences.

items.stem: Two miscible liquids in a binary mixture have boiling points of 65 degrees C and 100 degrees C. Considering vapor-pressure differences with temperature, which technique is most appropriate for separating them based on the boiling-point difference?
choices: Distillation, simple or fractional depending on the boiling-point gap
items.why: Distillation separates miscible liquids using their differing vapor pressures. A 35 degree gap usually allows simple distillation, but fractional distillation is preferred for narrower gaps or when high purity is required.

items.stem: A diethyl ether solution contains a neutral hydrocarbon, a phenol (pKa approximately 10), and a carboxylic acid (pKa approximately 4.5). Which aqueous wash selectively removes only the carboxylic acid into the aqueous layer, leaving the phenol and hydrocarbon in the organic layer?
choices: Saturated aqueous NaHCO3, which deprotonates only the carboxylic acid; the resulting carboxylate enters the aqueous phase
1 M NaOH, which would also deprotonate the phenol
items.why: Bicarbonate's effective pKa (around 6.4) is high enough to deprotonate carboxylic acids quantitatively but too low to deprotonate phenols. Selective deprotonation produces a water-soluble carboxylate, while the neutral phenol and hydrocarbon stay in the organic layer.

items.stem: An ether solution from a workup contains a desired neutral aromatic ester, a small carboxylic acid by-product (pKa approximately 4.5), and a phenol impurity (pKa approximately 10). Considering pKa selectivity and ester base-sensitivity, which aqueous wash extracts only the carboxylic acid?
choices: Wash with 1 M HCl (would not deprotonate carboxylic acid)
Wash with saturated NaHCO3, which deprotonates carboxylic acids selectively without hydrolyzing the ester or deprotonating the phenol
Distill the mixture and collect the highest-boiling fraction
Wash with 1 M NaOH, which would deprotonate the phenol and hydrolyze the ester
items.why: NaHCO3 has an effective base strength (pKa of H2CO3 approximately 6.4) sufficient to deprotonate carboxylic acids (pKa approximately 4-5) but not phenols (pKa approximately 10), and it is too weak to saponify esters. Only the acid moves into the aqueous layer.

items.stem: A chemist must purify a structurally homologous mixture of organic molecules that differ primarily in polarity (and only modestly in other physical properties). Which technique provides the highest resolution for separating compounds based on polarity at preparative scale?
choices: Column chromatography on silica gel with an organic eluent
items.why: Silica-gel column chromatography separates compounds by competitive adsorption: polar analytes interact more strongly with the polar stationary phase and elute later. Tuning eluent polarity allows resolution of analytes whose only meaningful difference is polarity.

items.stem: In the gas phase (no solvation), rank the basicity of the following anions/molecules toward a proton: an alkyl carbanion (R-CH2-), hydroxide (OH-), fluoride (F-), and ammonia (NH3). Which ordering correctly reflects intrinsic basicity?
choices: Alkyl carbanion > NH3 > OH- > F- (gas phase, decreasing electronegativity)
All four are equally basic in the gas phase
items.why: Basicity in the gas phase tracks inversely with conjugate-acid stability: alkanes (pKa ~50) are the weakest acids, so R-CH2- is the strongest base. Across a row, electronegativity rises (C < N < O < F), so the negative charge is least stabilized on carbon and most stabilized on fluorine.
items.skillName: acids and bases in ochem, concept

items.stem: Three molecules are dissolved in water at 25 degC: acetic acid (CH3COOH), ethanol (CH3CH2OH), and ethane (CH3CH3). Which contains the most acidic proton, and roughly what is its pKa?
choices: All three protons are similar in acidity
items.why: The acetic acid O-H (pKa ~4.76) is by far the most acidic because the conjugate base (acetate) is resonance-stabilized over two equivalent oxygens. Ethanol's alkoxide (pKa ~16) lacks resonance, and ethane's C-H (pKa ~50) leaves charge on carbon.

items.stem: Compare the C-H acidity of a terminal alkyne (HC≡C-R) to that of a vinyl C-H on an alkene (H2C=CHR). Which pair of approximate pKa values is correct, and which is more acidic?
choices: Both are ~25; they are equally acidic
Both are ~50; they are equally weak acids
Alkene ~25, alkyne ~44; the alkene is more acidic
Alkyne ~25, alkene ~44; the alkyne is more acidic
Alkyne ~10, alkene ~30; the alkyne is more acidic
items.why: Acidity tracks with s-character of the C-H bond: sp (50% s) holds the electron pair closer to the nucleus than sp2 (33% s). Terminal alkynes have pKa ~25, while vinyl C-H on alkenes is ~44.

items.stem: Among the three monohaloacetic acids X-CH2-COOH (X = F, Cl, Br) and acetic acid (CH3-COOH), which is the strongest acid in water? Inductive (through-sigma) electron withdrawal stabilizes the carboxylate.
choices: All four have nearly identical pKa values
items.why: Inductive withdrawal stabilizes the carboxylate conjugate base; the strongest -I effect at the alpha carbon comes from the most electronegative halogen. Fluorine is the most electronegative, so F-CH2-COOH (pKa ~2.6) is strongest, followed by Cl, Br, then unsubstituted acetic acid (pKa ~4.76).
items.skillName: acids and bases in ochem, concept

items.stem: In the gas phase (with solvation effects removed), arrange the following from STRONGEST to WEAKEST base toward a proton: an alkyl anion (R3C-), hydroxide (OH-), fluoride (F-), and the amide ion (NH2-).
choices: All four are equally strong bases
items.why: All four are anions on second-row atoms, so the deciding factor is electronegativity. Across the period it rises (C < N < O < F), and the more electronegative the atom, the better it tolerates the negative charge and the weaker it is as a base. The carbanion is therefore the strongest base and fluoride the weakest: alkyl > NH2- > OH- > F-.

items.stem: Sodium amide (NaNH2) deprotonates 1-hexyne (pKa ~25) cleanly but does not deprotonate vinyl C-H of 1-hexene (pKa ~44). The pKa gap is best explained by:
choices: Both protons are ~25; the difference is steric
Both protons are ~50; reactivity is kinetic
Alkene C-H is more acidic due to better resonance
Greater s-character of the sp alkyne carbon (50% vs 33%)
Inductive effect of the second pi bond raises alkene acidity
items.why: An sp-hybridized C-H bond holds bonding electrons closer to the carbon nucleus than sp2, stabilizing the conjugate base. Higher s-character means greater acidity, giving terminal alkyne pKa ~25 vs vinyl pKa ~44.

items.stem: Without solvation, which ordering of basicity is correct for an alkyl anion (R-), hydroxide (OH-), fluoride (F-), and ammonia (NH3)? Use trends down a row of the periodic table.
choices: Alkyl anion > NH3 > OH- > F- (intrinsic, gas phase)
All four are equally basic intrinsically
items.why: Within a row, the more electronegative atom holds negative charge better, weakening basicity. Carbon is the least electronegative of the four heavy atoms, so a carbanion is the strongest base; fluoride is the weakest.
items.skillName: acids and bases in ochem, concept

items.stem: Rank the intrinsic gas-phase basicity (without solvent) of these species from strongest to weakest: alkyl carbanion, NH3, OH-, F-. Which ordering reflects the periodic-trend ‘atom’ effect?
choices: Alkyl > NH3 > OH- > F- (less electronegative atoms hold charge more poorly)
items.why: Within a row, electronegativity rises C < N < O < F. The less electronegative the atom bearing the negative charge, the less it stabilizes that charge, so a carbanion is the strongest base in this set, and fluoride the weakest.
items.skillName: acids and bases in ochem, concept

items.stem: In aqueous solution at 25 degC, three compounds are present: acetic acid, ethanol, and ethane. Which compound contains the most acidic hydrogen, and what feature of its conjugate base accounts for the low pKa near 4.8?
choices: Acetic acid O-H, pKa ~5, resonance-delocalized carboxylate
Acetic acid alpha C-H, pKa ~25, enolate stability
items.why: Acetic acid's conjugate base (acetate) is stabilized by resonance over two equivalent oxygens, lowering its pKa to ~4.76. Ethanol's alkoxide has no such delocalization (pKa ~16), and ethane's C-H is essentially nonacidic (~50).

items.stem: Of the haloacetic acids F-CH2-COOH, Cl-CH2-COOH, Br-CH2-COOH, and unsubstituted acetic acid (CH3-COOH), which has the lowest pKa in water, and what stabilizes its conjugate base?
choices: CH3-COOH; methyl group is mildly electron-donating
Br-CH2-COOH; large, polarizable Br stabilizes charge
Cl-CH2-COOH; chlorine balances size and electronegativity
F-CH2-COOH; the most electronegative halogen exerts the strongest -I effect
All four pKa values are within ~0.1 units
items.why: Through-sigma (inductive) withdrawal pulls electron density away from the carboxylate, stabilizing the negative charge. Fluorine is the most electronegative element, so F-CH2-COOH (pKa ~2.6) is the strongest acid in this list.

items.stem: Compare ethane (CH3CH3), ethanol (CH3CH2OH), and acetic acid (CH3COOH). Which proton is the most acidic, and what is the dominant stabilization of its conjugate base?
choices: Acetic acid O-H (pKa ~5); carboxylate resonance over two oxygens
Ethanol O-H (pKa ~16); alkoxide is least stable
Acetic acid alpha C-H (pKa ~25); enolate resonance
All three protons are equivalent in acidity
items.why: Acetate is delocalized over two equivalent oxygens, dramatically lowering acetic acid's pKa to ~4.76. Ethanol's alkoxide has no resonance (~16); ethane (~50) leaves charge on a single sp3 carbon.

items.stem: In the gas phase (intrinsic basicity, no solvent), rank an alkyl anion, the amide ion (NH2-), OH-, and F-. Use periodic-trend reasoning across a row of the periodic table.
items.why: Across a row, electronegativity climbs (C < N < O < F), and a more electronegative atom holds a negative charge more comfortably, which makes it a weaker base. The carbanion is therefore the strongest base and fluoride the weakest: alkyl > NH2- > OH- > F-.

items.stem: Benzoic acid (pKa ~4.2) is treated with one equivalent of aqueous NaOH at room temperature. Which best describes the outcome and the principle that drives equilibrium?
