choices: Forms sodium benzoate + water; Brønsted acid-base, equilibrium favors the weaker acid (water, pKa 15.7)
No reaction, since benzoic acid is too weak
Forms ethyl benzoate via Fischer esterification
items.why: Hydroxide (conjugate acid pKa ~15.7) is a strong enough base to fully deprotonate benzoic acid (pKa ~4.2). Equilibrium favors formation of the weaker acid/base pair, water and the resonance-stabilized benzoate.

items.stem: Acetic acid, ethanol, and ethane are dissolved in DMSO. Which has the most acidic proton, and which factor makes the largest contribution to the difference in acidity?
choices: Ethane C-H; sp3 hybridization of the resulting carbanion
Ethanol O-H; electronegative oxygen stabilizes the alkoxide
Acetic acid alpha C-H; the enolate is the most stable anion
All three protons are equivalent in acidity in DMSO
Acetic acid O-H; resonance delocalizes the carboxylate
items.why: Acetate's negative charge is delocalized over two equivalent oxygen atoms by resonance, lowering acetic acid's pKa to ~4.76. Ethoxide has no resonance (pKa ~16), and ethanide (~50) leaves charge on carbon.

items.stem: 1-pentyne (terminal alkyne) and 1-pentene are each treated with the same base. Why does NaNH2 cleanly deprotonate 1-pentyne but not the vinyl C-H of 1-pentene? Compare the relevant pKa values.
choices: Vinyl C-H is more acidic (~25) due to better resonance
Both pKa ~50; the difference is purely kinetic
Both pKa ~25; the outcome depends on solvent
Alkyne ~25, vinyl ~44; sp carbon has more s-character
Alkyne pKa ~10, due to strain in the triple bond
items.why: Higher s-character in the C-H bond holds electrons closer to carbon, stabilizing the conjugate base. The sp-hybridized terminal alkyne carbon (50% s) gives pKa ~25, while sp2 (33% s) leaves the vinyl C-H at ~44.

items.stem: Which statement correctly compares the C-H acidity of a terminal alkyne and a vinyl C-H of an alkene, and explains the trend on the basis of orbital hybridization?
choices: Vinyl C-H more acidic due to pi-system stabilization
Alkyne pKa ~25 vs alkene vinyl pKa ~44; sp (50% s-character) stabilizes the carbanion better than sp2 (33%)
items.why: Increased s-character pulls bonding electrons closer to carbon, stabilizing the conjugate base. sp (alkyne, 50% s) gives pKa ~25; sp2 (alkene, 33% s) gives ~44.

items.stem: Benzoic acid is dissolved in diethyl ether and shaken with a saturated aqueous NaOH layer. Predict the chemistry and the location of the organic acid after partitioning, considering pKa values (PhCOOH ~4.2; H2O ~15.7).
choices: No deprotonation; the acid stays in the ether layer
Fischer esterification gives ethyl benzoate in the ether layer
A benzoyl ether forms by SN2 displacement of hydroxide
Sodium benzoate forms and moves into the aqueous layer
The acid is reduced to benzaldehyde by the NaOH
items.why: Hydroxide (conjugate acid pKa 15.7) is strong enough to deprotonate benzoic acid (pKa 4.2). The ionic benzoate is highly water-soluble, so it migrates into the aqueous layer, a textbook acid-base extraction.

items.stem: In a vacuum (without water solvating ions), arrange these as bases from strongest to weakest: tert-butyl carbanion, NH3, OH-, F-. Indicate the dominant factor that explains the gas-phase ordering.
choices: F- > OH- > NH3 > carbanion (electronegativity stabilizes lone pair)
OH- > F- > NH3 > carbanion (size effect dominates)
All are equal in the gas phase
Carbanion > NH3 > OH- > F-; lower electronegativity destabilizes negative charge, raising basicity
items.why: Across a row, the more electronegative atom stabilizes negative charge better, lowering basicity. Carbon is least electronegative, so the carbanion is the strongest gas-phase base; fluoride, the most electronegative, is the weakest.
items.skillName: acids and bases in ochem, concept

items.stem: HF (pKa ~3) is roughly 47 pKa units more acidic than CH4 (pKa ~50). Both protons sit on second-row atoms. Which CARDIO factor (Charge, Atom, Resonance, Dipole/induction, Orbitals) most directly explains the dramatic difference?
choices: Atom, within the same row, F is much more electronegative than C, so F- holds the negative charge better than CH3-
items.why: Comparing acidity at heteroatoms in the same row, the dominant factor is the electronegativity of the atom holding negative charge. Fluoride is far better at carrying that charge than methide, making HF orders of magnitude more acidic.

items.stem: HI (pKa ~ -10) is far more acidic than HF (pKa ~3), even though F is much more electronegative than I. Which CARDIO factor accounts for HI being the stronger acid?
choices: Down a column: I- is larger and more polarizable, spreading charge over a bigger volume
Different formal charges on the conjugate bases
items.why: Within a column of the periodic table, atomic size dominates over electronegativity for charge stabilization. The much larger I- spreads negative charge over a greater volume, making it a far weaker base than F-, so HI is more acidic.

items.stem: Phenol (PhOH, pKa ~10) is roughly 6 pKa units more acidic than cyclohexanol (pKa ~16), even though both are O-H acids whose oxygen is bonded to a six-membered ring carbon. The 6-unit gap is best ascribed to:
choices: Resonance: phenoxide spreads its charge into the ring
The more electronegative oxygen atom in phenol
Different formal charges on the two conjugate bases
Inductive donation from the methylene groups in cyclohexanol
Solvent effects that operate only in water
items.why: Phenoxide's negative charge is delocalized through the aromatic pi system to the ortho and para carbons by resonance, dramatically stabilizing it. Cyclohexanolate has no such delocalization, so its O-H is much less acidic.

items.stem: Trifluoroacetic acid (CF3COOH, pKa ~0.2) is about 4.5 pKa units stronger than acetic acid (pKa ~4.76). Both deprotonate at the same -COOH. The drop in pKa is best explained by:
choices: Resonance stabilization that's only present in trifluoroacetate
Inductive (through-sigma) electron withdrawal by the three highly electronegative fluorines, stabilizing the carboxylate
Hybridization change at the carbonyl carbon
A different atom holds the negative charge in trifluoroacetate
Differential solvation of CF3 vs CH3
items.why: Both acids deprotonate to a resonance-stabilized carboxylate; the structural difference is the alpha substituent. The three fluorines pull electron density through sigma bonds (-I), stabilizing the negative charge and lowering pKa.

items.stem: A terminal alkyne C-H has pKa ~25, while a vinyl alkene C-H has pKa ~44. Both involve C-H deprotonation to leave a carbanion on the same atom (carbon). The 19-unit gap is best assigned to which CARDIO factor?
choices: Resonance through the pi system of the triple bond
Charge, since the conjugate bases differ in formal charge
Atom, since the anion sits on a different element
Induction from the extra hydrogens on the vinyl carbon
Orbitals: sp carbon holds the lone pair closer than sp2
items.why: Same atom, no resonance involved on these C-H bonds, so the deciding factor is hybridization. Higher s-character means electrons are held closer to the nucleus, stabilizing the lone pair: alkyne (sp) is more acidic than alkene (sp2).

items.stem: The CARDIO mnemonic prioritizes factors that stabilize negative charge (and therefore raise acidity). Which of the following lists the priority in the correct order?
items.why: CARDIO ranks factors as: Charge (formal charge dominates), then Atom (electronegativity within a row, size within a column), then Resonance, then Dipole/Induction, then Orbital hybridization. Use the highest-priority discriminator that differs between two species.

items.stem: Glycine has -COOH (pKa1 ~2.3) and -NH3+ (pKa2 ~9.6). At physiological pH 7.4, which form predominates, and why?
choices: Cation (-NH3+, -COOH); pH below both pKa values
Zwitterion (-NH3+, -COO-); pH lies between the two pKa values, so the -COOH is deprotonated and the -NH3+ is still protonated
Anion (-NH2, -COO-); pH above both pKa values
Equal mix of all four forms
items.why: Henderson-Hasselbalch: a group is mostly deprotonated when pH > pKa and mostly protonated when pH < pKa. At pH 7, -COOH (pKa 2.3) is deprotonated to -COO-, and -NH3+ (pKa 9.6) remains protonated, giving the zwitterion.

items.stem: Solid sodium hydride (pKa of H2 ~36) is added to dry ethanol (pKa ~16) under nitrogen. Predict the outcome and the position of equilibrium.
choices: No reaction; NaH is too weak
Ethanol is fully deprotonated to sodium ethoxide; equilibrium strongly favors the forward direction (Keq ~10^20) and H2 gas evolves
NaH is protonated by ethanol; reverse reaction dominates
A new C-H bond forms on the ethyl carbon
items.why: Brønsted equilibrium favors the side with the weaker acid. Ethanol (pKa 16) is a far stronger acid than H2 (pKa 36), so the forward reaction is favored by ~20 pKa units; H2 gas escapes, driving the reaction.

items.stem: 2,4-pentanedione (CH3COCH2COCH3, acetylacetone) is treated with NaOEt. The most acidic proton (pKa ~9) is on which carbon, and why is it so acidic?
choices: Central CH2 between the two C=O groups; the resulting enolate is doubly resonance-stabilized over both carbonyl oxygens
An O-H tautomer is what is deprotonated
All hydrogens are equally acidic by symmetry
items.why: The CH2 sandwiched between two carbonyls forms an enolate that delocalizes its negative charge over both carbonyl oxygens. Double resonance stabilization drops the pKa to ~9, far more acidic than a single alpha C-H (~20).

items.stem: Ammonia is dissolved in pure water. Given pKa(NH4+) ~9.25 and pKa(H2O) ~15.7, what role does NH3 play, and roughly what fraction is protonated?
choices: Acts as a Brønsted acid by donating an N-H
Acts as a Brønsted base; equilibrium favors NH3 + H2O over NH4+ + OH- (Keq ~10^-4.7), but NH3 is the basic species in solution
Acts as both acid and base equally
Acts as a Lewis acid by accepting electrons from water
items.why: Comparing pKa values, NH3 deprotonates water only slightly (Kb small, ~1.8 x 10^-5), but the directionality is clear: NH3 is the base, abstracting H+ from H2O to give a small concentration of NH4+ and OH-. Hence aqueous NH3 is basic.

items.stem: Arrange the following anions by increasing basicity (weakest base first), using CARDIO logic: acetate (CH3COO-), methoxide (CH3O-), ethanide (CH3CH2-), acetylide (HC≡C-). Which is the STRONGEST base?
choices: Ethanide (CH3CH2-), pKa of conjugate acid ~50, sp3 carbanion
items.why: Strongest base = weakest conjugate acid. Conjugate-acid pKa values: acetic acid ~5, methanol ~16, acetylene ~25, ethane ~50. The largest pKa belongs to ethane, so its conjugate base (ethanide) is by far the strongest base.

items.stem: Boron trifluoride reacts with ammonia in the gas phase to form the adduct F3B-NH3. Identify the Lewis acid and the Lewis base, and explain the bonding.
choices: BF3 is the Lewis acid (empty p orbital); NH3 is the base
NH3 is the Lewis acid; BF3 donates a pair as the Lewis base
Both are Lewis acids, so no dative bond can form
Both are Lewis bases, and the product is an ionic salt
Neither; this is a Brønsted proton-transfer equilibrium
items.why: Lewis acid = electron-pair acceptor; Lewis base = electron-pair donor. BF3 has only six valence electrons on boron and an empty p orbital; NH3 has a lone pair on N. Donation from N into B forms a dative bond.
items.skillName: acids and bases in ochem, concept

items.stem: An IR spectrum shows a very broad O-H stretch from ~2500-3300 cm-1 superimposed on a sharp C=O stretch near 1710 cm-1. Which functional group best matches both features simultaneously?
items.why: Carboxylic acids show an extremely broad, dimer-H-bonded O-H stretch from ~2500-3300 cm-1 that often blankets the C-H region, plus a strong C=O near 1710 cm-1. Alcohols lack the C=O; amides show N-H instead of broad O-H.

items.stem: An IR spectrum of an unknown shows a sharp, medium-intensity peak at 2210 cm-1 with no broad features and no peak near 1700 cm-1. The functional group most consistent with this absorption is:
items.why: Triple bonds absorb in the 2100-2260 cm-1 region. Nitriles (C≡N) appear sharp around 2200-2260, while terminal alkynes (C≡C) are weaker and slightly lower (~2100-2150). The 2210 cm-1 peak fits a nitrile.

items.stem: A 1H NMR shows a triplet at 1.2 ppm (3H) coupled (J ~7 Hz) to a quartet at 3.7 ppm (2H), with no other multiplets nearby. The chemical shift of the quartet suggests an oxygen-bearing CH2. Which fragment is consistent?
items.why: Triplet/quartet (3H/2H) is the n+1 signature of an isolated -CH2-CH3 ethyl group. The OCH2 sits at 3.7 ppm because oxygen deshields it; the CH3 at 1.2 ppm is unaffected. Together they define an ethoxy (-OCH2CH3) fragment.

items.stem: A 13C NMR spectrum has a peak at 205 ppm with no peaks between 165-180 ppm. Which functional group accounts for the 205 ppm signal?
items.why: Aldehyde and ketone carbonyls appear furthest downfield in 13C, around 190-210 ppm. Esters, amides, and acids fall around 165-180 ppm because the heteroatom donates electron density to the carbonyl carbon, reducing deshielding.

items.stem: Compute the degrees of unsaturation (index of hydrogen deficiency) for the molecular formula C5H10. Use the formula DoU = (2C + 2 + N - H - X)/2.
choices: 2 (two rings or pi bonds, or a triple bond)
items.why: DoU = (2(5) + 2 - 10)/2 = 2/2 = 1. One degree of unsaturation means the molecule contains exactly one ring or one pi bond, for example, a pentene or a cyclopentane.

items.stem: Calculate the degrees of unsaturation for C6H5N (note: nitrogen contributes +1 in the numerator) using DoU = (2C + 2 + N - H - X)/2. What is the result, and what kind of structure could it represent?
choices: 6 (e.g., a benzene ring plus a C≡N)
items.why: DoU = (2(6) + 2 + 1 - 5)/2 = 10/2 = 5. Five degrees fit, for instance, an aromatic ring (4 DoU) plus an additional pi bond or ring. Always remember to add N in the numerator and subtract halogens.

items.stem: An EI mass spectrum shows a molecular ion at m/z 78 with an M+2 peak at m/z 80 of nearly equal (~1:1) intensity. The natural-abundance isotope ratio identifies which halogen?
items.why: Bromine's two stable isotopes (79Br and 81Br) are nearly equally abundant, giving an M/M+2 doublet at ~1:1. Chlorine gives 3:1, and fluorine and iodine are monoisotopic (no M+2 from the halogen).

items.stem: A 1H NMR of an unknown contains a singlet at 9.8 ppm integrating for one proton, plus a strong IR absorption at 1725 cm-1 and a band at 2720 cm-1. Which proton type is most consistent with the 9.8 ppm singlet?
items.why: Aldehyde protons resonate near 9.5-10 ppm because they are deshielded by the C=O group, and they often appear as a singlet (or weak doublet). The IR band at 2720 cm-1 (Fermi doublet with C-H stretch) plus 1725 cm-1 confirms an aldehyde.

items.stem: An IR spectrum of an aromatic unknown shows two strong peaks at ~1530 cm-1 and ~1350 cm-1 (sometimes called the ‘vampire-tooth’ pair). Which substituent is most consistent with this pattern?
items.why: Nitro groups have characteristic asymmetric and symmetric N-O stretches that appear as two strong bands near 1530 and 1350 cm-1. No other common group produces this distinctive ‘two-tooth’ pattern.

items.stem: Diethyl ether (CH3CH2-O-CH2CH3) is a symmetric ether with four total carbons. How many distinct 13C NMR signals does it show, and why?
choices: 2, the molecule has a mirror plane through the oxygen, so the two CH3's are equivalent and the two OCH2's are equivalent
items.why: Symmetric R-O-R molecules have a mirror plane through O. In diethyl ether the two methyl carbons are chemically equivalent and the two methylene carbons are equivalent, giving exactly two 13C signals.

items.stem: An unknown is treated with Tollens reagent (Ag(NH3)2OH in dilute base) at room temperature. A silver mirror deposits on the inside of the test tube. Which functional group is being identified, and what is being oxidized?
choices: Aldehyde (oxidized to carboxylate; Ag+ reduced to Ag0)
Methyl ketone (Tollens does not oxidize ketones)
items.why: Tollens reagent is a mild oxidant that converts aldehydes (R-CHO) to carboxylates (R-COO-) while reducing the silver complex to elemental silver, which deposits as a mirror. Ketones lack the C-H on the carbonyl and don't react.

items.stem: The iodoform test (I2 + aqueous NaOH) gives a yellow CHI3 precipitate. A positive result indicates the substrate contains either a CH3-C(=O)- group or a CH3-CH(OH)- group. Which class of compounds gives a positive iodoform test?
choices: All carbonyl compounds, including esters and amides
Carboxylic acids and their esters only
items.why: The iodoform reaction tri-iodinates the alpha-methyl of a methyl ketone (or methyl carbinol oxidized first). NaOH then cleaves the C-CI3 bond, releasing yellow CHI3 (iodoform). Substrates without a -COCH3 (or -CH(OH)CH3) cannot form CHI3.

items.stem: Bromine in CCl4 (orange-red) is added dropwise to four separate samples in the dark. The orange color disappears within seconds for which substrate, indicating addition across the pi bond?
items.why: Br2 in CCl4 undergoes electrophilic addition across alkene/alkyne pi bonds at room temperature without catalyst, consuming Br2 and decolorizing the solution. Alkanes need light/heat (radical), aromatics need Lewis acid, and alcohols don't react.

items.stem: On a normal-phase TLC plate (silica = polar stationary phase) developed with a nonpolar mobile phase such as hexane/ethyl acetate (90:10), where does the most polar compound in a mixture end up after development?
choices: Travels furthest from the baseline (highest Rf) with the solvent
Stays near the baseline (lowest Rf), held by the polar silica
Does not interact with the plate and moves with the solvent front
Runs off the top edge of the plate during development
Becomes invisible under UV light after development
items.why: ‘Like dissolves like’ on TLC: polar compounds bind tightly to polar silica and resist being carried along by a nonpolar solvent, giving low Rf values. Less polar species are pulled along with the solvent front and have higher Rf.

items.stem: You need to separate two miscible organic liquids by simple distillation at atmospheric pressure. The technique works most cleanly when:
choices: Boiling points are within 5 degC of each other
Boiling points differ by more than about 25 degC
Both components have identical boiling points (azeotrope)
Neither liquid boils below its decomposition temperature
One component is a solid at room temperature
items.why: Simple distillation relies on a meaningful vapor-pressure difference. If the boiling points differ by less than ~25 degC, the vapor over the boiling mixture is too rich in both components and a fractional column is required for clean separation.

items.stem: An ether solution contains both a carboxylic acid (pKa ~4) and a phenol (pKa ~10). To selectively pull only the carboxylic acid into the aqueous layer (leaving the phenol in ether), which aqueous wash is best?
choices: Saturated NaHCO3 (pKa of H2CO3 ~6.4): deprotonates the COOH (pKa 4) but not the phenol (pKa 10)
items.why: Bicarbonate is basic enough to deprotonate carboxylic acids (pKa ~4) but not phenols (pKa ~10), since the conjugate acid H2CO3 has pKa 6.4. Only the carboxylate is ionized and partitions into water, leaving the phenol in ether.

items.stem: Recrystallization is the standard method for purifying a crystalline organic solid. Which choice best describes the procedure and the principle that delivers pure crystals?
choices: Boil away all of the solvent leaving the solid behind
Dissolve the impure solid in a minimum of hot solvent, then cool slowly so that the major component crystallizes selectively while small amounts of impurity remain in the cold mother liquor
Mix the solid with sand and filter
items.why: Recrystallization exploits the solubility difference between hot and cold solvent. Slow cooling allows the major (high-concentration) species to nucleate and form a clean crystal lattice, while trace impurities at low concentration remain dissolved and are washed away.

items.stem: Gas chromatography (GC) separates volatile components passed through a heated column with a stationary phase. The primary physical property responsible for separation order is:
choices: Polarity alone, with no temperature dependence
Boiling point (volatility): lower-boiling components elute first because they spend less time in the liquid stationary phase
Molecular weight as the only determinant
items.why: GC separates by partitioning between mobile gas and the liquid stationary phase. Compounds with lower boiling points have higher vapor pressure, partition less into the stationary phase, and elute earlier. (Polarity matters only in the choice of stationary phase.)

items.stem: Jones reagent (CrO3 in aqueous H2SO4/acetone) is added to 2-pentanol (a secondary alcohol) at 0 degC. The major product is:
choices: 2-pentanone (a ketone), Jones cleanly oxidizes 2 deg alcohols to ketones
Pentanoic acid (over-oxidation product, requires 1 deg alcohol)
items.why: Secondary alcohols have only one alpha hydrogen on the carbinol carbon, so oxidation stops at the ketone. Jones cannot oxidize a 2 deg alcohol further (no remaining alpha-H). Primary alcohols, in contrast, would go all the way to the carboxylic acid under aqueous Jones.

items.stem: 1-butanol is independently treated with (a) PCC in dry CH2Cl2 and (b) Jones reagent (CrO3/H2SO4 aq). Which reagent stops cleanly at the aldehyde, and why?
choices: Both stop at the aldehyde under these conditions
Jones, because the aqueous acid conditions favor the aldehyde
PCC, since anhydrous conditions block hydrate formation
Neither; both continue on to the carboxylic acid
Only KMnO4 would stop at the aldehyde stage
items.why: Over-oxidation of an aldehyde requires hydration of the C=O to a gem-diol, which Cr(VI) then re-oxidizes to a carboxylic acid. PCC is run in anhydrous CH2Cl2, so the aldehyde never hydrates and the reaction halts cleanly. Jones is aqueous and proceeds to the acid.

items.stem: An ether solution contains a carboxylic acid (pKa ~4), a phenol (pKa ~10), and aniline (an aromatic amine, conjugate acid pKa ~4.6). After washing with saturated aqueous NaHCO3, which compound remains in the ether layer?
choices: Carboxylic acid (it's deprotonated and pulled into water)
Phenol (NaHCO3 is too weak a base to deprotonate phenol, pKa 10, so phenol stays in ether)
Aniline (it's a base; NaHCO3 wouldn't ionize it anyway, but the question asks who NaHCO3 leaves behind, both phenol and aniline stay; among the listed single answers, phenol is the cleanest)
All three end up in the aqueous layer
All three remain in the ether layer
items.why: NaHCO3 (conjugate acid pKa 6.4) deprotonates the carboxylic acid (pKa 4) and pulls it into water, but it's too weak to deprotonate the phenol (pKa 10). The neutral phenol stays in ether. Aniline is a base and is unaffected by bicarbonate, so it also stays in ether.

items.stem: A Diels-Alder cycloaddition is run between a 1,3-diene and an electron-poor dienophile in toluene at 80 degC. Which conformation must the diene adopt to undergo the [4+2], and why is the alternative geometrically forbidden?
choices: s-trans, because the termini are far apart
s-cis, so the two terminal carbons can simultaneously bond to the two dienophile carbons in a single concerted pericyclic step
items.why: Diels-Alder is a concerted suprafacial-suprafacial [4+2] requiring both ends of the diene to reach the dienophile at once. Only the s-cis conformer places those termini close enough; s-trans is too elongated.

items.stem: 1,3-butadiene reacts with maleic anhydride (a strong dienophile) in xylene at reflux. Predict the product and the relative stereochemistry, considering the suprafacial-suprafacial nature of the Diels-Alder cycloaddition.
choices: An open-chain ester with cis double bonds
cis-4-cyclohexene-1,2-dicarboxylic anhydride (the two anhydride substituents end up cis on the new six-membered ring; endo selectivity favored)
items.why: Diels-Alder is a syn (suprafacial) addition on both partners, so the two anhydride substituents on maleic anhydride remain cis on the newly formed cyclohexene ring. The C=C between C4-C5 of the new ring is retained.

items.stem: Cold, dilute aqueous KMnO4 (basic conditions, ~0 degC) is added to cyclohexene. The major organic product is:
choices: Cyclohexanone, from oxidation at one carbon
items.why: Cold, dilute KMnO4 forms a cyclic manganate ester across one face of the alkene, then hydrolyzes to deliver both OH groups to the same face, a syn-diol. Hot/concentrated KMnO4 instead cleaves to carbonyls.

items.stem: 2-methyl-2-butene is treated with O3 in CH2Cl2 at -78 degC, then with Zn/AcOH (reductive workup). Identify the two carbonyl products formed by cleavage across the trisubstituted alkene.
choices: Acetone + acetaldehyde (the more substituted side gives a ketone; the less substituted side gives an aldehyde)
Two molecules of acetic acid (oxidative workup)
items.why: Ozonolysis cleaves the C=C, replacing each carbon's substituents with =O. The 2-substituted side (CMe2) becomes acetone; the 3-CH(CH3) side becomes acetaldehyde. Reductive workup (Zn/AcOH or Me2S) prevents oxidation of the aldehyde.

items.stem: Cyclohexene is treated with N-bromosuccinimide (NBS) in CCl4 with a low constant concentration of Br2 (radical chain) under hv at room temperature. Identify the regiochemistry of the bromine atom in the major product.
choices: Br adds across both alkene carbons (1,2-dibromide)
Br is installed at the allylic position (C3, next to C=C); the alkene is preserved
Br ends up on a random vinyl carbon
No reaction without a Lewis acid catalyst
items.why: NBS/hv generates a low concentration of Br• that selectively abstracts the weakest C-H, the allylic position, giving a resonance-stabilized allyl radical. The radical then traps Br• to form 3-bromocyclohexene; the C=C is retained.

items.stem: 1-methylcyclohexene is subjected to hydroboration-oxidation: BH3·THF at 0 degC, then aqueous NaOH/H2O2. What is the major alcohol, including stereochemistry?
items.why: Hydroboration is anti-Markovnikov (boron goes to the less substituted C) and syn (B and H on the same face). Oxidative workup retains stereochemistry, replacing B with OH. On 1-methylcyclohexene this places OH on C2 trans to the C1 methyl.

items.stem: 2-pentyne is hydrogenated using H2 over Lindlar's catalyst (Pd/CaCO3 poisoned with Pb(OAc)2 and quinoline) in EtOAc at 1 atm. The major product is:
choices: (Z)-2-pentene (cis alkene; H2 delivered syn from one face of the surface and the reduction halts at the alkene)
An equilibrium mixture of cis and trans alkenes
items.why: Lindlar is a deactivated Pd catalyst that delivers H2 syn to the same face of the alkyne and is poisoned enough that further reduction of the alkene is suppressed. The result is a Z (cis) alkene.

items.stem: 2-pentyne is treated with sodium metal in liquid ammonia at -33 degC. After workup, the major alkene product is:
choices: (E)-2-pentene (trans, from dissolving-metal reduction via radical anion intermediate)
items.why: Dissolving-metal reduction (Na/NH3(l)) proceeds through a vinyl radical anion that adopts the more stable trans geometry before being protonated by ammonia. The result is a stereospecifically E (trans) alkene.

items.stem: An aldehyde is stirred with two equivalents of methanol in the presence of a catalytic acid (p-TsOH) under Dean-Stark conditions to remove water. Which functional group is the final isolated product?
items.why: Acid-catalyzed addition of one equivalent of ROH gives the hemiacetal; loss of water (driven by the Dean-Stark trap) and a second ROH addition installs the second alkoxy group, yielding an acetal. Acetals are stable under base and serve as carbonyl protecting groups.

items.stem: Cyclohexanone is treated with pyrrolidine (a secondary amine) and a catalytic amount of p-TsOH in benzene at reflux with a Dean-Stark trap. The product is:
choices: An enamine (the nitrogen is bonded to the alpha-carbon analog; pi bond between alpha-C and former carbonyl C)
items.why: Secondary amines lack a second N-H, so the iminium intermediate cannot tautomerize to a neutral C=N. Instead, an alpha-proton is lost to form a C=C-N enamine, with water removed by Dean-Stark.

items.stem: Acetophenone (PhCOCH3) is heated with one equivalent of methylamine (a primary amine) in benzene with catalytic AcOH and a Dean-Stark trap to remove water. Identify the major product.
choices: Imine (Schiff base): PhC(=NMe)CH3, formed by condensation and loss of H2O
items.why: Primary amines have two N-H bonds. After nucleophilic addition gives the hemiaminal, water is eliminated and the second N-H is lost to give a neutral C=N (imine, Schiff base). Secondary amines instead form enamines.

items.stem: Sodium borohydride (NaBH4) in methanol at 0 degC is added to a flask containing one of each functional group below. Which subset of carbonyls does NaBH4 reduce, and which does it leave untouched?
choices: Reduces aldehydes, ketones, and acid chlorides cleanly; does NOT reduce esters, carboxylic acids, or amides
items.why: NaBH4 is a mild hydride source: strong enough to attack highly electrophilic C=O of aldehydes, ketones, and acid chlorides, but too weak for esters, amides, and carboxylic acids (which need LiAlH4). It tolerates protic solvents like methanol.

items.stem: A primary amide R-C(=O)NH2 is reduced with excess LiAlH4 in dry diethyl ether at 0 degC, then aqueous workup. The product is:
choices: Aldehyde R-CHO (would require a milder controlled reduction such as DIBAL at -78 degC)
Alcohol R-CH2-OH (this is the LiAlH4 product of an ester or acid)
items.why: LiAlH4 reduces amides all the way to amines: hydride attacks C=O, the nitrogen pushes out -O- to give an iminium, and a second hydride reduces the iminium to a CH2-NR group. Net: -C(=O)-NR2 -> -CH2-NR2.

items.stem: Phenylmagnesium bromide (PhMgBr) is added to acetonitrile (CH3CN) in dry ether at 0 degC, then the reaction mixture is treated with aqueous H3O+. The final product is:
choices: A primary amine, PhCH2NH2, from reduction
A tertiary alcohol, from double addition
Benzoic acid, from hydrolysis of the nitrile
items.why: Grignards add once to nitriles, giving an N-Mg ketimine intermediate. Aqueous acidic workup hydrolyzes the imine to a ketone. The carbon from the nitrile becomes the carbonyl carbon, and the alkyl/aryl from the nitrile becomes one substituent.

items.stem: Methylenetriphenylphosphorane (Ph3P=CH2, an unstabilized Wittig ylide) is added to cyclohexanone in THF at room temperature. Identify the products.
choices: An acetal, from addition of two oxygens
A tertiary alcohol, after aqueous workup
A carboxylic acid, from ring opening
items.why: The Wittig reaction joins the carbonyl carbon to the ylide carbon and ejects the oxygen as Ph3P=O via a four-membered oxaphosphetane, replacing C=O with C=C. Unstabilized ylides typically give the Z-alkene; on a ketone like cyclohexanone, geometry doesn't apply.

items.stem: A weak (soft) nucleophile such as a cuprate or a stabilized enolate is added to methyl vinyl ketone (CH2=CH-C(=O)CH3) at -78 degC. Which carbon does it attack, and what is this regiochemistry called?
choices: The alpha carbon (between the carbonyl and the beta carbon)
The beta carbon (1,4-/conjugate/Michael addition); soft nucleophiles are reversible at C=O and prefer the thermodynamic conjugate adduct
items.why: Hard nucleophiles (RLi, RMgX) attack the carbonyl carbon in a 1,2-fashion; soft nucleophiles add reversibly at C=O but irreversibly at the beta carbon (1,4-addition, Michael). The resulting enolate then tautomerizes to the saturated ketone.

items.stem: 2-methylcyclohexanone has two distinct alpha positions. It is treated with one equivalent of LDA in THF at -78 degC. Which enolate predominates, and what is the principle?
choices: The thermodynamic (more substituted) enolate, because it is more stable
The kinetic (less substituted) enolate, because LDA is a bulky, strong, non-nucleophilic base that selectively removes the more accessible (less hindered) alpha-H at low temperature
items.why: LDA's large isopropyl groups disfavor abstraction of a hindered alpha-H. At -78 degC the kinetic deprotonation is locked in (no equilibration), giving the less-substituted (kinetic) enolate. Higher T or weaker bases give the more stable thermodynamic enolate.

items.stem: Which substrate gives a positive iodoform test (yellow CHI3 precipitate) when treated with I2 and aqueous NaOH at 0 degC?
choices: A methyl ketone (R-COCH3) or methyl carbinol (R-CH(OH)CH3), base-catalyzed alpha-iodination of the CH3 followed by hydroxide cleavage of the C-CI3 bond
items.why: The iodoform reaction tri-iodinates the alpha methyl, then NaOH cleaves the C-CI3 bond to give a carboxylate plus yellow CHI3. Only -COCH3 (methyl ketones, acetaldehyde) or methyl carbinols (which oxidize first under the conditions) qualify.

items.stem: An aldol reaction between two molecules of acetaldehyde (NaOH, H2O) is heated above 60 degC. Beyond the initial beta-hydroxy aldehyde, what is the dehydration product?
choices: alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl (enone/enal); E1cb dehydration eliminates water across alpha-beta to give the conjugated product (crotonaldehyde here)
items.why: Heating an aldol drives E1cb dehydration: the alpha-H is removed (acidic due to the new beta-OH adjacent C=O), and -OH leaves, giving conjugation between C=C and C=O, an alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl. Conjugation provides the thermodynamic driving force.

items.stem: Two equivalents of ethyl acetate are treated with sodium ethoxide in dry ethanol, then quenched with aqueous acid. Identify the type of product formed by this Claisen condensation.
choices: A beta-keto ester (ethyl acetoacetate, CH3COCH2COOEt), one ester's enolate displaces the OEt of a second ester
items.why: In a Claisen, an alpha-deprotonated ester attacks the carbonyl of a second ester; the alkoxide (-OEt) then leaves, yielding a beta-keto ester. The product is acidic (pKa ~11) and is deprotonated by ethoxide, driving equilibrium forward.

items.stem: Ethyl acetoacetate (CH3COCH2COOEt) is treated with NaOEt, then ethyl iodide, then aqueous NaOH (saponification), then heat. The acetoacetic ester synthesis builds substituted:
choices: Methyl ketones (the final beta-keto acid loses CO2 via a 6-membered TS, leaving R-CH2-COCH3)
Carboxylic acids (that's the malonic ester synthesis)
items.why: Acetoacetic ester synthesis: alkylate the central CH2, then saponify the ester to a beta-keto acid that decarboxylates on heat (6-membered TS), leaving a methyl ketone bearing the new R group at the alpha carbon.

items.stem: Diethyl malonate (CH2(COOEt)2) is treated with NaOEt, then n-propyl iodide, then aqueous NaOH (saponification), then heat. The malonic ester synthesis builds substituted:
choices: Carboxylic acids, the resulting malonic acid loses one CO2 via a 6-membered TS, leaving a single -COOH bearing the new alkyl group
items.why: Malonic ester synthesis: alkylate the central CH2 (pKa ~13 due to flanking esters), saponify both esters to a malonic diacid, and heat. One -COOH decarboxylates via a 6-membered TS, leaving R-CH2-COOH, a substituted carboxylic acid.

items.stem: A beta-keto acid (e.g., acetoacetic acid, CH3COCH2COOH) is heated to ~120 degC in an inert solvent. What is the principal transformation, and what is the geometric requirement?
choices: Decarboxylation to lose CO2 via a six-membered cyclic transition state in which the carboxylic O-H is shuttled to the carbonyl oxygen, forming an enol that tautomerizes to a methyl ketone (acetone)
items.why: The beta-keto group is positioned to accept the -COOH proton through a six-membered TS, allowing concerted loss of CO2 and formation of an enol. The enol tautomerizes to the more stable keto form. This is why acetoacetic and malonic ester syntheses end with heat.

items.stem: A molecule contains three stereogenic centers and no internal symmetry (no meso form). Using 2^n, what is the MAXIMUM possible number of distinct stereoisomers?
items.why: Each stereocenter contributes a factor of 2 (R or S), so the maximum count is 2^n. With n=3 centers and no symmetry to fold pairs into meso compounds, the molecule has 2^3 = 8 distinct stereoisomers (4 pairs of enantiomers).

items.stem: Tartaric acid has two stereogenic centers but only three stereoisomers total. The third compound is called the meso form. Which statement best characterizes a meso compound?
choices: Achiral overall despite containing stereogenic centers, due to an internal mirror plane (the two halves are mirror images of each other within the same molecule)
items.why: A meso compound contains stereocenters but is superimposable on its mirror image because of an internal mirror plane. The local rotations cancel and the molecule is optically inactive, different from a racemate, which is a 1:1 mixture of two enantiomers.

items.stem: A solution contains a 50:50 mixture of (R)- and (S)-2-bromobutane (a racemic mixture). Light from a sodium D line (589 nm) is passed through a polarimeter cell of fixed length. The observed optical rotation is:
choices: A positive rotation equal to that of either pure enantiomer
0 deg, because the two rotations cancel exactly
A negative rotation, half that of a pure enantiomer
A value that depends linearly on total concentration
No value, because a racemate cannot be measured
items.why: Each enantiomer rotates plane-polarized light by an equal magnitude in opposite directions. With equal concentrations (50:50), the rotations cancel exactly, giving an observed rotation of 0, the defining feature of a racemic mixture.

items.stem: (Z)- and (E)-2-butene differ only in the spatial arrangement around the C=C double bond. They are not mirror images of each other. The most accurate classification of this stereochemical relationship is:
choices: Diastereomers (stereoisomers that are not mirror images)
items.why: Cis (Z) and trans (E) alkene isomers have identical connectivity but different spatial arrangements; they are not mirror images of each other (each is achiral). Stereoisomers that are not enantiomers are diastereomers, and they have different physical properties.

items.stem: On a Fischer projection, the lowest CIP priority group (often H) is on a horizontal line, which means it points TOWARD the viewer. Reading priorities 1->2->3 traces out a clockwise circle on paper. What is the true R/S designation, and why?
choices: S, because the lowest priority points toward you, so you must invert the apparent rotation
Cannot be determined from a Fischer projection
items.why: CIP requires the lowest-priority group to point AWAY from the viewer. If it points toward you, the directly read rotation is reversed: clockwise on paper actually corresponds to S, and counterclockwise corresponds to R.

items.stem: Two diastereomers of a chiral natural product are isolated. Compared with each other, which physical/chemical properties typically differ?
choices: Only the sign of optical rotation; everything else is identical
Most physical properties, boiling point, melting point, solubility, density, IR/NMR, and reactivity, because diastereomers are not mirror images and have different internal energies
Only the wavelength of UV absorption
items.why: Diastereomers differ in spatial arrangement but are not mirror images, so their internal interactions (steric, dipole, H-bonding) differ. That gives different boiling/melting points, solubilities, NMR shifts, and even different reaction rates, unlike enantiomers, which differ only in chiral environments.

items.stem: Hückel's rule states a flat, fully-conjugated, cyclic system is aromatic when it has 4n+2 pi electrons. Cyclobutadiene is square planar, fully conjugated, and has 4 pi electrons. How is cyclobutadiene best classified, and what does that imply for its stability?
choices: Anti-aromatic (4 pi electrons, 4n with n=1) and destabilized, even less stable than the open-chain analog
Aromatic but only at low temperature
items.why: A planar, fully conjugated cyclic system with 4n pi electrons (here 4) is anti-aromatic by Hückel's rule. Cyclobutadiene is destabilized relative to its non-cyclic dienyl reference, it actually distorts to a rectangular geometry to minimize anti-aromatic destabilization.

items.stem: Nitrobenzene (PhNO2) is treated with Br2/FeBr3 at 0 degC. The nitro group is a strong sigma-withdrawing AND pi-withdrawing substituent. Where does the new Br substituent end up, and why?
choices: Meta (1,3-disposition); the NO2 destabilizes the ortho/para sigma-complex by placing positive charge directly on the carbon bearing -NO2
items.why: Strongly deactivating substituents (NO2, CN, COR, COOH, SO3H, NR3+) destabilize the arenium ion when the new substituent goes ortho or para, the cation rests on a carbon bearing the EWG. The meta product avoids that, so EAS is meta-selective (and slow).

items.stem: Nitrobenzene is treated with acetyl chloride and AlCl3 (standard Friedel-Crafts acylation conditions) in CH2Cl2 at 0 degC. What is the result?
choices: No reaction, the strongly deactivating -NO2 makes the ring too electron-poor for Friedel-Crafts (acylation OR alkylation) to proceed
Yes, but only at high temperature (>200 degC)
Forms an N,N-acyl product on the nitrogen
items.why: Friedel-Crafts reactions fail on rings bearing strong deactivators (-NO2, -CN, -SO3H, -NR3+, -CF3) because the ring is too electron-poor to attack the acylium ion. They also fail on -NH2 rings because the amine ties up AlCl3 (Lewis acid quenching).

items.stem: Halogens (-F, -Cl, -Br, -I) are unusual EAS substituents because they show one effect inductively and the opposite effect through resonance. In EAS bromination of chlorobenzene, the regiochemistry and rate are best described as:
choices: Deactivate (-I dominates rate) but direct ortho/para (+M lone pair stabilizes the sigma-complex when the new group is ortho/para)
items.why: Halogens are sigma-withdrawing through induction (slowing the reaction) but pi-donating through resonance via the lone pair (giving ortho/para selectivity). The two effects partially cancel, so halobenzenes react in EAS slower than benzene but with ortho/para regiochemistry.

items.stem: An aryl diazonium salt (ArN2+ Cl-) prepared at 0 degC from an aniline + NaNO2/HCl is treated with CuBr (a Sandmeyer reagent). The major product is:
choices: Ar-OH, from hydrolysis of the diazonium in warm water
Ar-CN, from a Sandmeyer cyanation of the salt
Ar-H, from reduction of the diazonium salt
Ar-Br, from copper(I)-mediated replacement of N2
Ar-Ar, from radical coupling of two aryl groups
items.why: Sandmeyer reactions use Cu(I) salts to replace -N2+ on the ring: CuBr -> ArBr; CuCl -> ArCl; CuCN -> ArCN. They proceed via a single-electron transfer mechanism that releases N2 gas. CuI does not work, KI is used instead.

items.stem: Toluene (PhCH3) is heated with hot, concentrated KMnO4 (aqueous, ~100 degC) for several hours and then acidified. What is the organic product?
choices: Benzoic acid (PhCOOH); side-chain oxidation cleaves all benzylic C-H bonds and installs a -COOH directly on the ring
items.why: Hot KMnO4 oxidizes any alkyl group with at least one benzylic C-H all the way to a carboxylic acid attached directly to the ring, regardless of original chain length. Tert-butyl groups (no benzylic H) are inert. Toluene -> benzoic acid.

items.stem: Given starting materials and curved arrows shown, predict the SN2 product.
items.why: HO− attacks the carbon backside, displacing Br−. Product: methanol + bromide.

items.stem: 2-Bromobutane + KOEt (concentrated, hot). Arrows show concerted E2. What is the major Zaitsev product?
items.why: Strong base + concentrated conditions favor E2 with Zaitsev orientation. Anti-periplanar geometry favors trans.

items.stem: The carbonate ion has the Lewis structure shown with curved arrows indicating resonance. What is the correct major contributor?
choices: One C=O and two C-O⊖, in three equivalent forms
Three C=O double bonds on one carbon
One C=O, one C-O⊖, and one neutral C-OH
C with three single bonds and triple negative charge
Two C=O and one C-O⊖, with carbon bearing 5 bonds
items.why: Carbonate has three equivalent resonance structures with one C=O and two C-O⊖ each; arrows show electron-pair movement between equivalent contributors.

items.stem: Propene + HBr. Arrows show electrophilic addition forming the more stable carbocation. Predict the major product.
items.why: Electrophilic addition: π electrons attack H, forming the more stable secondary carbocation. Br− then attacks the 2° carbon → 2-bromopropane.

items.stem: tert-butyl chloride converts to tert-butanol in aqueous solution (SN1). Given the starting material and product below, which curved-arrow set correctly describes the rate-determining step?
choices: One arrow from H2O lone pair to C with simultaneous C-Cl breakage (concerted)
Two arrows: one from H2O to C, one from C-Cl to Cl, both at the same time
No arrows needed, since the step is only a proton transfer
One arrow from an O-H bond to O, deprotonating the oxonium ion
One arrow from the C-Cl bond to Cl, generating t-Bu+ and Cl−
items.why: SN1 RDS = unimolecular ionization. The single arrow from C-Cl bond to Cl produces a tertiary carbocation. Water attack is the fast second step.

items.stem: 3-methyl-2-butanol + HBr (excess). Arrows show carbocation formation and subsequent hydride shift. Predict the major product.
items.why: Protonation of the OH and loss of water gives a secondary carbocation at C2. A 1,2-hydride shift from C3 turns it into the more stable tertiary cation, and bromide traps that carbon to give 2-bromo-2-methylbutane. 2-Bromo-3-methylbutane is the unrearranged product, 2-methyl-2-butene is an E1 alkene that excess HBr would convert to the same bromide, and the two 1-bromo isomers put bromine on a primary carbon that never carries the positive charge.

items.stem: Benzene + Br2 / FeBr3. The mechanism shows electrophile generation followed by aromatic π-attack. Which set of arrows correctly describes BOTH steps?
choices: 1 arrow: the arene π bond attacks Br2 directly, no catalyst
3 arrows: arene π to Br, Br-Br to FeBr3, FeBr3 to Br
2 arrows: Br-Br bond to FeBr3, then arene π bond to Br+
No arrows, since the bromination is a radical chain
2 arrows: Br+ to the arene π bond, then FeBr3 to Br-Br
items.why: EAS = combined mechanism. Step 1 generates Br+ via Lewis-acid activation. Step 2 arene π attacks the electrophile, breaking aromaticity at the sigma-complex.

items.stem: (R)-2-bromobutane is treated with sodium hydroxide in DMSO at 25°C. The major organic product is an alcohol, and the reaction follows second-order kinetics with rate = k[substrate][NaOH]. Which of the following best describes the product and the mechanism?
items.why: Second-order kinetics in a polar aprotic solvent with a 2° substrate and a strong nucleophile points to SN2. Backside attack inverts the stereocenter: (R) → (S).

items.stem: A student wants to convert 1-methylcyclohexene into trans-2-methylcyclohexan-1-ol with anti-Markovnikov regiochemistry. Which two-step sequence accomplishes this transformation?
items.why: Hydroboration-oxidation gives anti-Markovnikov OH addition with syn stereochemistry, placing OH on the less substituted carbon, opposite of oxymercuration.

items.stem: A compound with molecular formula C5H10O shows the following 1H NMR: a triplet at 1.06 ppm (3H), a singlet at 2.13 ppm (3H), and a quartet at 2.45 ppm (2H). The IR spectrum shows a strong absorption at 1715 cm−1 and no broad O-H stretch. Identify the compound.
items.why: IR at 1715 cm−1 with no broad O-H stretch confirms a ketone. The 1H NMR shows a triplet at 1.06 ppm (3H, CH3), a singlet at 2.13 ppm (3H, CH3CO), and a quartet at 2.45 ppm (2H, CH2). This three-signal pattern with those integrations matches 2-pentanone (methyl propyl ketone): CH3-CO-CH2CH2CH3, where the terminal methyl and adjacent CH2 give the triplet/quartet, and the acetyl CH3 gives the singlet.

items.stem: Toluene is treated with concentrated nitric acid in the presence of concentrated sulfuric acid at 50°C. After workup, the reaction mixture contains predominantly two regioisomers in roughly 60:40 ratio along with a small amount of a third. Which two products dominate and why?
choices: meta- and para-nitrotoluene; methyl is a weak meta director
ortho- and para-nitrotoluene; methyl is an o/p director (activator)
meta- and ortho-nitrotoluene; methyl directs by hyperconjugation only
ortho- and meta-nitrotoluene; methyl is a deactivator
items.why: CH3 is an activating ortho/para director via hyperconjugation. Nitration gives ~60% para and ~40% ortho with traces of meta.

items.stem: Cyclohexanone is added dropwise to a chilled solution of phenylmagnesium bromide in dry diethyl ether under nitrogen. After the addition is complete, the reaction is quenched with saturated NH4Cl(aq). What is the major product?
items.why: Grignard adds to the carbonyl C, generating a tertiary alkoxide. Aqueous workup protonates to give the tertiary alcohol 1-phenylcyclohexan-1-ol.

items.stem: Rank the following compounds in order of INCREASING acidity (least acidic first): CH3CH3 (ethane), CH3OH (methanol), CH3COOH (acetic acid), CH3SO3H (methanesulfonic acid), and HC≡CH (acetylene).
items.why: pKa values: ethane ~50, acetylene ~25, methanol ~16, acetic acid ~4.8, methanesulfonic acid ~−2. Acidity increases left to right; the conjugate base resonance/inductive stabilization dominates.

items.stem: A compound with the structure (2R, 3S)-2,3-dichlorobutane is heated. Its mirror image is (2S, 3R)-2,3-dichlorobutane. Which statement correctly describes the relationship between these two molecules and any internal symmetry?
choices: They are enantiomers; the molecule is chiral and optically active
They are diastereomers; they have different physical properties
They are the SAME meso compound; the internal mirror plane makes the molecule achiral and optically inactive
They are constitutional isomers; the connectivity differs
They are conformers; rotation around C2-C3 interconverts them
items.why: (2R,3S) has an internal mirror plane between C2 and C3 that swaps R↔S → meso. The "mirror image" is identical to itself; meso compounds are achiral despite having stereocenters.

items.stem: Propose a 3-step synthesis of 2-methylpentan-2-ol starting from 2-bromopropane. Step 1: Mg, dry ether. Step 2: react with X. Step 3: aqueous workup. What is reagent X?
items.why: Step 1 makes isopropylmagnesium bromide. Adding it to butan-2-one (CH3COCH2CH3) gives a tertiary alcohol: HO-C(CH3)(C(CH3)2H)CH2CH3 = 2-methylpentan-2-ol after workup. Acetone would give 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol; propanal would give a secondary alcohol.

items.stem: 2-chloro-2,3-dimethylbutane is dissolved in 80% ethanol/20% water and gently warmed. The reaction follows first-order kinetics. Among the products is a tertiary alcohol that is NOT the simple substitution product of the original carbon. Which mechanism best explains this observation?
choices: SN2 with backside displacement on the secondary carbon
SN1 with a 1,2-methyl shift forming a more stable tertiary carbocation, then water attack
E1cb deprotonation generating an enolate intermediate
Direct radical-chain substitution via a chlorine radical
items.why: First-order kinetics + tertiary halide + protic solvent = SN1. The initial 3° cation can undergo 1,2-methyl shift to give an even more stable cation; water attack at the new center yields a rearranged tertiary alcohol.

items.stem: Two molecules of acetone undergo a base-catalyzed self-aldol condensation followed by dehydration upon heating. The aqueous NaOH first deprotonates an alpha hydrogen; the resulting enolate attacks the carbonyl of a second acetone molecule. What is the major final product after dehydration?
items.why: Self-aldol of acetone: enolate of one acetone attacks the carbonyl of another → 4-hydroxy-4-methylpentan-2-one. Heat drives dehydration of the β-hydroxy ketone to the α,β-unsaturated ketone mesityl oxide.

items.stem: You compare the 13C NMR spectra of two C8H10 isomers: para-xylene and ortho-xylene. Based purely on molecular symmetry, how many UNIQUE carbon environments would each compound exhibit?
items.why: p-xylene has D2h symmetry: the two ring carbons bearing CH3 are equivalent, the four other ring carbons are pairwise equivalent (2), and the two methyls are equivalent (1) → 3 unique. o-xylene has C2v symmetry: 4 unique aromatic environments + 1 unique methyl = 4 unique total. Higher symmetry → fewer peaks.

items.stem: Rank the following four amines in order of DECREASING basicity in aqueous solution: pyridine, aniline, ammonia, and triethylamine.
items.why: Aliphatic 3° amine (Et3N, pKaH ~10.7) > NH3 (pKaH ~9.25) > pyridine (pKaH ~5.2, sp2 N pulls lone pair into the ring) > aniline (pKaH ~4.6, lone pair conjugates into the aromatic ring).

items.stem: A chemist performs Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene using tert-butyl chloride and AlCl3 to make tert-butylbenzene. The reaction works in good yield. However, when the same chemist attempts the same reaction on nitrobenzene, no product forms even after extended heating. Which factor best explains the failure?
choices: The nitro group strongly deactivates the ring (resonance withdrawal); the resulting arenium intermediate cannot form
The nitro group reacts preferentially with AlCl3, consuming the Lewis acid
Friedel-Crafts alkylation requires alkenes, not alkyl halides
tert-butyl cation rearranges before substitution can occur
items.why: Nitro is a strong −M deactivator. It depletes electron density from the ring and destabilizes the arenium (sigma-complex) intermediate so much that Friedel-Crafts alkylation effectively fails.

items.stem: A student isolates a mixture of benzoic acid (pKa ≈ 4.2), 2-naphthol (pKa ≈ 9.5), and naphthalene (neutral) in dichloromethane. They wish to separate all three using acid-base extraction with two aqueous solutions. Which order of washes correctly extracts the carboxylic acid first and the phenol second?
choices: Wash 1: 1 M NaOH (extracts both); wash 2: 1 M HCl (re-extracts phenol)
Wash 1: saturated NaHCO3 (extracts carboxylic acid only); wash 2: 1 M NaOH (extracts phenol)
Wash 1: 1 M HCl (extracts amine); wash 2: saturated NaHCO3 (extracts phenol)
Wash 1: saturated NaCl (salts out carboxylic acid); wash 2: NaOH (extracts naphthalene)
Wash 1: 1 M NaOH (extracts naphthalene); wash 2: 1 M HCl (extracts both acids)
items.why: NaHCO3 deprotonates carboxylic acids (pKa < 6) but not phenols (pKa ~10). NaOH then deprotonates the phenol. Naphthalene stays in DCM.

items.stem: A Diels-Alder reaction is performed between (E,E)-2,4-hexadiene and maleic anhydride. The reaction is concerted, suprafacial on both components, and proceeds through a single cyclic transition state. Which statement about the stereochemistry of the cyclohexene product is CORRECT?
choices: The two methyl groups end up trans on the cyclohexene ring; the anhydride carbonyls are syn (endo)
The two methyl groups end up cis on the cyclohexene ring; the anhydride is also cis to them (endo)
All substituents end up trans; this is a [4+2] anti-suprafacial process
The product is a 1:1 mixture of cis and trans methyl groups
The reaction does not proceed because (E,E)-dienes cannot reach the s-cis conformation
items.why: Concerted Diels-Alder preserves dienophile and diene stereochemistry: (E,E)-diene gives cis methyls on the new ring; maleic anhydride (cis dienophile) gives cis ester groups; endo rule typically dominates kinetically.

items.stem: (2S,3S)-3-bromo-2-butanol is treated with concentrated HBr at 50 °C. The product is identified as (2S,3R)-2,3-dibromobutane (a meso compound). Which mechanism best accounts for both the regiochemistry and the loss of optical activity?
choices: SN2 with backside attack at C2 inverting that center while C3 is unchanged
SN1 via a bridged bromonium ion at C2-C3 followed by anti-periplanar attack of Br⁻ at C2
Pinacol rearrangement followed by Br⁻ capture
Two sequential SN2 steps with double inversion
items.why: Neighboring-group participation by Br at C3 forms a bridged bromonium intermediate. Br⁻ opens it from the backside at C2, inverting C2 and giving the (2S,3R) meso diastereomer.

items.stem: A compound with molecular formula C₉H₁₀O₂ shows: IR 1715 cm⁻¹ (no broad O–H); ¹H NMR singlet 3.85 ppm (3H), AA'BB' pattern 7.85 (2H) and 6.92 (2H), singlet 2.55 (3H); ¹³C shows 5 unique aromatic carbons. Identify the compound.
items.why: Para substitution → AA'BB' aromatic pattern (4 H total appearing as two doublets). 1715 cm⁻¹ is methyl ketone, not ester (esters ~1735–1745). The 3.85-ppm OMe singlet + 2.55 ppm methyl ketone fit p-methoxyacetophenone (DOU=5; 5 unique aromatic C's due to p-symmetry).

items.stem: A chemist needs meta-bromonitrobenzene from benzene. Two single-step routes are tried: (i) Br₂/FeBr₃ then HNO₃/H₂SO₄, or (ii) HNO₃/H₂SO₄ then Br₂/FeBr₃. Which gives the desired meta isomer in good yield, and why does the other route fail?
choices: (i) works; the methyl ortho/para directs nitration meta
(ii) works; nitro is a meta director, so subsequent bromination installs Br meta
Neither works; meta-bromonitrobenzene must be made via diazonium chemistry
(i) works because Br is a meta director; (ii) fails because nitrobenzene cannot brominate
items.why: Install the strong meta director (NO₂) FIRST. Subsequent bromination of nitrobenzene proceeds (slowly) at the meta position. Route (i) installs Br first (an ortho/para director), so nitration ends up ortho/para to Br rather than meta.

items.stem: A symmetric ketone is treated with LDA (1 equiv) at −78 °C in THF, then methyl iodide is added. Workup gives an alpha-methylated ketone with high regioselectivity for the LESS substituted alpha carbon (kinetic enolate). Which combination of features explains why LDA at low T gives the kinetic product instead of the thermodynamic one?
choices: LDA is small and nucleophilic; it adds to the carbonyl rather than removes the alpha proton
LDA is sterically bulky and a strong, non-nucleophilic base; low T prevents enolate equilibration to the more stable substituted enolate
LDA generates radicals that abstract H from the less hindered C
Low T accelerates the more-substituted enolate formation via tunneling
LDA is acidic, protonating the more-substituted alpha C
items.why: Bulky, non-nucleophilic base + low T → rapid, irreversible deprotonation at the most accessible alpha H = kinetic enolate at the less substituted side. Thermodynamic conditions (NaH, room T) would give the more substituted enolate.

items.stem: A molecule has three stereocenters and ONE internal mirror plane that bisects the central C and exchanges the other two stereocenters. How many distinct stereoisomers does the molecule have, and how many of them are optically active?
items.why: Internal mirror plane reduces 2³ = 8 to 4 unique configurations. Pairs related by the mirror plane collapse: (RRR ↔ SSS pair active enantiomers), (RSR = meso, achiral), (SRS = meso, achiral). So 4 distinct stereoisomers, 2 optically active.

items.stem: Compare the gas-phase acidity (deprotonation energy) of CH₃CO₂H and CF₃CO₂H to their aqueous-phase acidity (pKa). In which phase is the inductive effect of the −CF₃ group MORE dominant in determining the relative acidity, and why?
choices: Aqueous phase; water solvation amplifies the inductive effect
Gas phase; without solvent, the only stabilization of the conjugate base is intrinsic (inductive/resonance), so the substituent effect is larger in magnitude
Both phases are equally affected, pKa differences mirror gas-phase ΔE
Inductive effects only operate in the gas phase; in water they vanish
Aqueous phase; the trifluoromethyl group H-bonds to water
items.why: In the gas phase the conjugate base has no solvation, so substituent stabilization (inductive of CF₃) dominates the ΔE. In solution, water stabilizes the carboxylate so much that intrinsic substituent effects are partially leveled, hence smaller pKa differences than gas-phase trends would suggest.

items.stem: Treatment of (E)-2-butene with mCPBA followed by aqueous acid yields one diastereomer of 2,3-butanediol almost exclusively. Identify the product and the stereochemical reason.
choices: (2R,3S) meso compound; epoxide opens with anti (trans) addition of OH groups, giving overall syn-addition appearance from a trans-alkene
(2R,3R)/(2S,3S) racemate; trans-alkene → trans-diol via concerted syn epoxidation followed by anti opening
A single optically active enantiomer; mCPBA is chiral
items.why: mCPBA epoxidizes (E)-2-butene to a (2R,3R) / (2S,3S) trans-epoxide racemate. Acid opens the epoxide via SN2-like backside attack of water → anti opening; combined with the trans starting material the net diol is the (2R,3R)/(2S,3S) racemate (both stereocenters inverted at one carbon).

items.stem: In an SN1 solvolysis of 3-chloro-3-methyl-1-butene in aqueous ethanol, two products form: 3-methyl-3-buten-2-ol and 2-methyl-3-buten-2-ol, in roughly 60:40 ratio. What best explains the formation of BOTH products from the same intermediate?
choices: A single allylic carbocation is delocalized across two carbons; nucleophile attacks at either resonance position
A radical chain mechanism with two propagation pathways
The starting material isomerizes before ionization
Carbocation rearrangement via methyl shift forms a new structure entirely
items.why: Ionization gives an allylic cation with positive character on both ends of the π-system. Water attack at either resonance center gives the two regioisomeric alcohols.

items.stem: You need to synthesize a compound containing exactly ONE primary alcohol AND ONE tertiary alcohol on the same skeleton, starting from acetone and an alkyl Grignard. Which 3-step strategy works and gives high yield?
choices: (1) Grignard adds to acetone → tertiary alcohol; (2) protect with TMS-Cl/imidazole; (3) hydroboration-oxidation of a separate alkene to install the primary OH; deprotect.
Open an epoxide with the Grignard (gives 1° alcohol on one chain) then add the resulting Mg-alkoxide intramolecularly to acetone for the 3° alcohol, single pot.
Cannot be done, Grignards are basic and would deprotonate any alcohol formed
Reduce acetone to 2-propanol with NaBH4, then etherify to install primary alcohol
items.why: Sequence: Grignard → 3° alcohol; protect; install 1° alcohol via independent hydroboration-oxidation; deprotect. The protection step is mandatory, Grignards or strong bases would otherwise destroy alcohols formed earlier.

items.stem: Which compound shows the LARGEST chemical-shift downfield (highest ppm) for the indicated proton in ¹H NMR? Choose the proton that experiences the strongest deshielding from a combination of electronegativity, anisotropy, and resonance-induced positive character.
choices: The terminal vinyl H of styrene
The CO₂H proton of acetic acid
items.why: Carboxylic acid O–H typically appears as a very broad signal at 11–13 ppm, by far the most deshielded common proton due to strong H-bonding plus the electron-poor O. Aldehydic H is next (~9.7).

items.stem: In acidic aqueous solution at pH 1, which compound exists predominantly as its CATIONIC conjugate-acid form? (Use approximate pKaH: pyridine 5.2, aniline 4.6, methylamine 10.6, imidazole 7.0, pyrrole −3.8.)
choices: Methylamine, pyridine, aniline, imidazole, all four protonated; pyrrole remains neutral
Only methylamine is protonated; the others are neutral at pH 1
All five compounds are protonated at pH 1
Aniline alone is protonated; the rest are too weakly basic
Pyrrole and pyridine are protonated; methylamine and aniline are not
items.why: A base is mostly protonated when pH < pKaH. At pH 1: methylamine (10.6 ✓), imidazole (7.0 ✓), pyridine (5.2 ✓), aniline (4.6 ✓) are all protonated. Pyrrole (pKaH = −3.8) requires pH < −3.8 to protonate, so it stays neutral.

items.stem: A student runs TLC of a mixture of three compounds: a carboxylic acid, an alcohol, and a hydrocarbon. They use silica gel (polar stationary phase) with hexane:ethyl acetate (4:1) as the mobile phase. Which compound has the LARGEST Rf value (travels furthest), and why?
choices: Carboxylic acid; it ionizes and elutes quickly
Hydrocarbon; it interacts least with the polar stationary phase, so it spends the most time in the mobile phase
All three travel together (same Rf) because polarity is irrelevant in TLC
Carboxylic acid; it has the largest molecular weight so it diffuses fastest
items.why: On polar silica, the LEAST polar compound interacts least with the stationary phase and is carried farthest by the non-polar mobile phase. Hydrocarbon → highest Rf; carboxylic acid (most polar) → lowest Rf.

items.stem: Compare the relative rates of E2 elimination for three substrates with the same alkyl-halide skeleton: 1-bromobutane, 2-bromobutane, and 2-bromo-2-methylpropane, with concentrated KOC(CH₃)₃ in t-butanol. Rank by E2 rate (fastest first).
choices: 3° > 2° > 1° (more β-H availability and more stable alkene products)
items.why: Bulky base strongly favors E2. Rate increases with substrate substitution: more β-H positions and the resulting alkene is more substituted (more stable). 3° > 2° > 1°. The bulky base also suppresses competing SN2.

items.stem: Phenol is brominated with Br₂ in water (no Lewis acid needed) to give 2,4,6-tribromophenol. Why does this aromatic substrate require neither FeBr₃ nor any other Lewis-acid catalyst, and why does TRI-bromination occur in a single reaction even though aromatic rings normally over-substitute only on activated rings?
choices: Phenol is highly activated; the OH lone pair donates strongly into the ring, generating sufficient electrophile (Br⁺) reactivity without a Lewis acid. Each successive Br adds activation, leading to 2,4,6-tribromination
Phenol is deactivated; tribromination is anomalous
Water acts as the Lewis acid catalyst
Phenol carries a net negative charge in water
Br₂ rapidly hydrolyses to HOBr, which alone can brominate
items.why: OH is a strong activator (resonance donor). The ring is electron-rich enough that polarized Br–Br cleaves heterolytically without Lewis-acid help. Each substitution still leaves a strongly activated ring, so substitution proceeds 2× more (ortho and para available) until the 2,4,6 positions are all brominated.

items.stem: When propanoic acid reacts with thionyl chloride (SOCl₂), then ammonia, then heat with P₂O₅ to dehydrate, the final product is a nitrile. Identify the nitrile and explain why each step is needed.
choices: Propanenitrile (CH₃CH₂CN); SOCl₂ activates COOH → acid chloride; NH₃ converts to primary amide; P₂O₅ dehydrates amide to nitrile
Acetonitrile (CH₃CN), one carbon is lost during dehydration
Hydrocyanic acid (HCN); the propyl chain is lost
items.why: COOH → COCl (SOCl₂) → CONH₂ (NH₃) → CN (dehydration with P₂O₅). Three carbons retained: propanenitrile.
